title: Bicentric comparison of 3-year clinical outcomes between endoscopic ultrasound-guided embolization with coil and hemostatic adjunct versus balloon-occluded retrograde transvenous obliteration for treatment of bleeding gastric varices: A propensity-score matched study.
abstract: Background and aims Endoscopic ultrasound-guided coil injection (EUS-COIL) and balloon-occluded retrograde transvenous obliteration (BRTO) performed by interventional radiology (IR) are both effective obliterative procedures to treat gastric varices. Comparative studies are lacking. Our aim was to assess clinical outcomes for EUS-COIL versus BRTO for treatment of acute gastric variceal bleeding. Methods This retrospective cohort study included all patients admitted to two tertiary care centers between 2009-2024 who underwent either EUS-COIL or BRTO for bleeding gastric varices. The primary outcomes were technical/clinical success and adverse events. Secondary outcomes included transfusions, reintervention, length of hospital stay, further hepatic decompensation (esophageal variceal hemorrhage, new ascites, or new hepatic encephalopathy (HE)), and all-cause mortality. Subgroup analyses were performed in patients with cirrhosis, including with propensity score matching (PSM) which was conducted 1:1 for age, sex, Child-Pugh classification, MELD-Na score, and hemoglobin level on admission. Outcomes over the 36-months post-intervention were assessed using time-to-event analysis. Results A total of 94 patients were included (48 EUS-COIL, 46 BRTO), of whom 60 patients with cirrhosis (30 per group) were analyzed after propensity score matching. In the matched cohort, technical success was 100% in both groups and clinical success was 100% versus 93.3% (p=0.49). The EUS-COIL group experienced significantly fewer adverse events (3% vs 37%; p=0.003) and had a longer time-to-reintervention (65 ± 52 days vs 10 ± 9.6 days; p=0.022) over a median follow-up 900 ± 790 days. The incidence of further hepatic decompensation was lower in the EUS-COIL group (10% vs 40%; p=0.007), as was the likelihood of further hepatic decompensation (HR 0.28 (95%CI: 0.08-0.984), p = 0.047) compared to BRTO. No significant differences were observed with regard to post-procedural transfusion requirements, rates of reintervention, length of hospital stay, and mortality in cirrhosis patients. In the unmatched cohort, technical (100% vs 80%; p=0.001) and clinical (100% vs 89%; p=0.03) success were higher with EUS-COIL than BRTO. Conclusions In patients with gastric variceal hemorrhage, EUS-COIL demonstrated higher rates of technical/clinical success and lower rates of adverse events (both peri-procedural and on long-term follow-up) compared to BRTO. EUS-COIL had significantly lower rates of further hepatic decompensation. While larger prospective studies are required, these data suggest that EUS-COIL, when available, may be the preferred initial therapy for bleeding gastric varices as part of a step-up strategy.

title: Incidence and Follow-Up of Extracardiac Findings on Cardiac Computed Tomography: A Single Tertiary Centre Experience.
abstract: Background Extracardiac findings (ECF) are frequently detected on cardiac computed tomography (CT), yet their clinical follow-up in contemporary practice is variable. We sought to describe their incidence and assess whether clinically significant findings were associated with documented follow-up or further investigation. Method We conducted a retrospective observational study of consecutive patients undergoing cardiac CT, including CT coronary angiograms (CTCA) and CT left atrial mapping (CTLA), at a single tertiary centre between January 2021 and December 2022. ECF data were extracted from formal reports. For patients with clinically significant findings, electronic medical records were reviewed to determine whether findings were documented as acknowledged and whether further investigation or follow-up was recorded. Results A total of 402 patients underwent cardiac CT. Most ECF were low risk, including hiatus hernia (39.8%) and small pulmonary nodules <6 mm (13.4%). Clinically significant ECF were identified in 41 patients (10.2%), including pulmonary nodules measuring 6-8 mm (2.7%), pulmonary nodules >8 mm (2.5%), indeterminate liver lesions (1.5%), other mass lesions (1.5%), and pulmonary emboli (1.2%). Twenty-two patients (5.5%) met criteria for Fleischner guideline-directed surveillance, of whom 15 had documented follow-up, including one subsequent diagnosis of malignancy. Overall, 12 patients (29.2%) with clinically significant ECF had no documented follow-up. Clinically significant ECF were more frequently observed in patients undergoing CTLA (odds ratio 2.4; 95% confidence interval 1.1-5.1; p=0.03) and were associated with higher odds of lacking documented follow-up compared with CTCA (odds ratio 4.8; 95% confidence interval 1.1-21.2; p=0.05). Missed clinically significant ECF predominantly occurred in the outpatient setting. Conclusions ECF on cardiac CT are common, and approximately 10% represent clinically significant abnormalities. In this cohort, clinically significant findings identified on CT left atrial mapping were associated with lower rates of documented follow-up compared with CTCA. These findings suggest a potential vulnerability in outpatient CTLA mapping pathways and support consideration of strategies to reduce unacknowledged ECF.

title: Impact of hepatocellular carcinoma proximity to the hepato-caval confluence on the recurrence risk after hepatectomy.
abstract: Background The prognostic impact of HCC proximity to major hepatic veins is unclear. We studied whether tumour distance to the inferior vena cava (IVC) or suprahepatic veins (SHV) influences recurrence and survival after resection. Methods Retrospective single-centre cohort of consecutive HCC resections (2012-2021). To limit confounding, 70 patients with moderately aggressive tumours (AFP < 1000 ng/mL), size < 150 mm, no preoperative macrovascular invasion and R0 resection were analysed. Distance to vessel (DTV) on preoperative CT scan (minimum HCC-IVC/SHV) classified patients as DTV ≤ 10 mm or > 10 mm. Primary endpoint disease-free survival (DFS); secondary: overall survival (OS). Cox models adjusted for covariates. Results Baseline characteristics were similar between the two groups, with a median follow-up of 56 months. Median DFS was shorter in DTV ≤ 10 mm: 28 vs 40 months (p = 0.04). In multivariable analysis, DTV ≤ 10 mm (HR 1.88; p = 0.028) and higher preoperative MELD (HR 1.25; p = 0.0001) independently predicted poorer DFS. Median OS tended to be lower with DTV ≤ 10 mm (70 vs 117 months; p = 0.06). Conclusion HCC proximity ≤ 10 mm to SHV/IVC is associated with higher recurrence risk and a trend to worse OS after R0 resection. Prospective validation is warranted.

title: Temporal Changes in LGE-CMR Enhancement After Monopolar Biphasic Focal Pulsed Field Ablation for Pulmonary Vein Isolation.
abstract: Background Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has emerged as a novel non-thermal ablation modality for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) in atrial fibrillation (AF). While chronic lesion formation after PFA has been described, data regarding acute lesion characteristics and lesion maturation remain limited. Objective To characterize acute and chronic lesion formation following focal point-by-point PFA for PVI using serial late-gadolinium-enhancement cardiovascular-magnetic-resonance-imaging (LGE-CMR). Methods Six consecutive patients with symptomatic paroxysmal or persistent AF underwent index PFA-guided PVI using the CENTAURI system and a focal point-by-point lesion delivery strategy. LGE-CMR was performed 1 day and 90±10 days after ablation. Quantitative assessment of regional and global left atrial (LA) enhancement was performed using a standardized segmentation protocol. Changes in enhancement burden and LA dimensions were analyzed between imaging timepoints. Results Among six patients at mean age 65±7 years, five patients (83%) had paroxysmal AF. Acute PVI was achieved in all patients without procedural complications. Serial LGE-CMR demonstrated substantial temporal changes between acute and chronic imaging. Enhancement within the right pulmonary vein (PV) region decreased from 3.3±2.2% to 0.8±0.8%(p=0.030), while the proportion of enhanced tissue decreased from 24.1±13.5% to 5.7±5.8%(p=0.017). Similar reductions were observed around the left PVs (4.4±3.1%vs.1.4±1.2%, p=0.064). Posterior wall enhancement decreased from 2.4±1.1% to 0.3±0.3%(p=0.007) and global LA enhancement from 12.8±6.2% to 3.3±1.6%(p=0.013), while LA volume remained unchanged. Conclusion Serial LGE-CMR demonstrated substantial enhancement reduction of acute lesions following focal point-by-point PFA for PVI, which remained largely confined to the PV antra and adjacent posterior wall, providing novel in-human insights into lesion maturation following focal PFA delivery.

title: The triglyceride-glucose index and intramyocardial hemorrhage identify a high-risk phenotype in STEMI.
abstract: Aims The prognostic value of combining the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH) in STEMI is unclear. We assessed their individual and combined association with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Methods This retrospective study included 456 STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI. TyG index was calculated from admission blood samples; IMH was assessed by cardiac magnetic resonance. The primary outcome was MACE (median follow-up 4 years). Multivariable Cox regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, incremental prognostic assessment (C-index, NRI, IDI), and interaction testing were performed. Results MACE increased across TyG tertiles (15.79% → 27.63% → 43.42%). The highest tertile remained independently associated with MACE (adjusted HR 1.86; 95% CI 1.09-3.20). Patients with high TyG (≥8.66) plus IMH had the worst prognosis (HR 4.00; 95% CI 2.49-6.39; P < 0.001), far exceeding either factor alone. Adding the combined variable to a base model improved discrimination and reclassification (C-index 0.640 → 0.658; NRI = 0.216, P = 0.020; IDI = 0.025, P = 0.008). Neither additive nor multiplicative interaction was significant, and results were consistent in diabetic and non-diabetic patients. A significant interaction was observed between TyG index and infarct location (P for interaction = 0.037), with a stronger effect in anterior (HR 1.59) than non-anterior infarction (HR 0.75). Conclusions The TyG index independently predicts long-term MACE in STEMI. Combining high TyG with IMH identifies a high-risk phenotype with a 4.0-fold higher MACE risk and incremental prognostic value. The TyG effect is stronger in anterior infarction, suggesting infarct location should be considered in metabolic risk stratification.

title: Radiotherapy and brachytherapy capacity, treatment timelines, and barriers to guideline-concordant curative care for cervical cancer in Latin America: the LATAM-CxRT study.
abstract: Objective To describe national radiotherapy and brachytherapy capacity, treatment delivery, and barriers to guideline-concordant curative treatment among women with cervical cancer requiring definitive or adjuvant radiotherapy in Latin America. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional survey of national radiation oncology coordinators from 14 Latin American countries using a standardized Research Electronic Data Capture questionnaire covering institutional mix, radiotherapy and brachytherapy infrastructure, imaging capacity, cervical cancer caseloads, external beam radiotherapy and brachytherapy practice, treatment timelines, and barriers and needs as perceived by coordinators. Data were cross-checked against International Atomic Energy Agency and vendor data where available. Results Fourteen countries contributed data: all completed general characteristics, 13 completed the resources and workforce module, and 12 completed the full equipment and timelines module. Among these 12 countries, the median number of linear accelerators was 33.5 per country (interquartile range 9 to 101.75), reflecting a right skew driven by Brazil. The median annual caseload was 680.5 patients for International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stages I to II disease and 800 patients for stages III to IV disease. Nearly all countries reported intensity-modulated radiotherapy, image-guided radiotherapy, and volumetric-modulated arc therapy capabilities. Gynecologic high-dose-rate brachytherapy was available in all 12 countries, although several reported insufficient coverage, with services concentrated in reference centers; magnetic resonance imaging-guided brachytherapy, interstitial techniques, and anesthesia support were available in only a subset. Half of countries reported 91% to 100% brachytherapy completion among women initiating curative chemoradiation, but overall treatment time from external beam radiotherapy start to brachytherapy completion exceeded 56 days in most countries. To describe national radiotherapy and brachytherapy capacity, treatment delivery, and barriers to guideline-concordant curative treatment among women with cervical cancer requiring definitive or adjuvant radiotherapy in Latin America.

We conducted a cross-sectional survey of national radiation oncology coordinators from 14 Latin American countries using a standardized Research Electronic Data Capture questionnaire covering institutional mix, radiotherapy and brachytherapy infrastructure, imaging capacity, cervical cancer caseloads, external beam radiotherapy and brachytherapy practice, treatment timelines, and barriers and needs as perceived by coordinators. Fourteen countries contributed data: all completed general characteristics, 13 completed the resources and workforce module, and 12 completed the full equipment and timelines module. This 14-country survey demonstrates that, despite widespread availability of advanced external beam radiotherapy, cervical cancer care in Latin America remains constrained by heterogeneous and often insufficient brachytherapy and imaging resources and by treatment delays exceeding guideline recommendations. title: Artificial Intelligence for Triage in Primary Care: A Scoping Review of Clinical Applicability.
abstract: Aim To map artificial intelligence (AI) systems developed for triage in primary care and describe their characteristics, performance and clinical applicability. Methods A scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, MEDLINE (via Ovid), Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL (via EBSCOhost), IEEE Xplore and the ACM Digital Library were searched until March 14th 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data on system characteristics, triage function, performance, validation, safety, equity and implementation. Each system was charted by triage function and by whether it was patient-facing, clinician-facing or fully automated. Results Seventeen studies were included, published between 2013 and 2026 across 12 countries (14/17 high-income). Most were clinician-facing decision support (14/17), three had a patient-facing component and none were autonomous. Diagnostic or screening triage was the most common function (n = 7), followed by prioritisation (n = 4) and referral routing (n = 4). Only two performed urgency classification or self-triage. As a clinician aid, AI improved performance (fundus accuracy 82.8 % to 91.1 %; dermoscopy management sensitivity 72.9 % to 94.2 %), but standalone models sometimes fell below clinicians. Reported accuracy ranged from 41.2 % to 98.28 % and AUROC from 0.65 to 0.90, on heterogeneous outcomes. Validation was mostly internal (11/17), external in four. None reported a prospective randomised comparison or measured patient outcomes. Conclusion AI triage in primary care is concentrated on clinician-facing diagnostic and referral tasks and is most valuable for augmenting clinician workflows, particularly non-specialists. The evidence base remains immature, constrained by internal validation, unreliable reference standards, sparse equity assessment and absent prospective outcome data. Future work should prioritise prospective, outcome-anchored evaluation, with attention to safety and equity.

title: Profile and classification of invasive fungal disease in patients with haematologic malignancies using microscopy, culture, biomarkers and polymerase chain reaction.
abstract: Background Invasive fungal diseases (IFDs) are significant causes of morbidity and mortality in patients with haematologic malignancies (HM). This study aimed to classify IFD using integrated diagnostic methods according to European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer/Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium (EORTC/MSGERC) criteria. Methods A prospective observational study was conducted in 100 adult HM patients not on antifungal prophylaxis. Diagnosis included microscopy, culture, galactomannan (GM) enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), Candida mannan immunoglobulin M (IgM) lateral flow assay (LFA), Aspergillus IgM assay, cryptococcal antigen LFA, (1,3)-β-D-glucan (BDG) assay and panfungal polymerase chain reaction (PCR), along with high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT). Results Probable IFD was observed in 51%, possible in 24%, proven in 12% and no IFD in 13%. Acute leukaemia predominated, with invasive aspergillosis (IA) and candidiasis being the most common infections. Fever was the most frequent presentation, while respiratory symptoms were associated with invasive aspergillosis. PCR showed the highest sensitivity (88.8%), followed by BDG (87.3%). Microscopy and culture were positive in 25% cases, Aspergillus fumigatus being the most common isolate. HRCT was normal in 56%, with ground-glass opacities and consolidation as the most frequent abnormalities. Conclusion Integrated diagnostic approaches improve classification and early detection of IFD in HM patients and support timely antifungal management.

title: Is technical difficulty associated with the accuracy of patient-specific implants for maxillary repositioning in minimally invasive orthognathic surgery?
abstract: The use of patient-specific implants (PSIs) in minimally invasive orthognathic surgery remains limited due to concerns about technical difficulty and restricted intraoperative exposure. Whether increasing maxillary movement technical difficulty compromises the accuracy of PSI-assisted minimally invasive surgery remains unclear. This retrospective cohort study evaluated the accuracy of maxillary repositioning using PSIs in minimally invasive bimaxillary orthognathic surgery and its relationship to technical difficulty. Consecutive patients treated at the University of Texas Health San Antonio between June 2023 and September 2025 were included if they underwent bimaxillary minimally invasive orthognathic surgery with complete preoperative and postoperative cone-beam computed tomography records. Patients with craniofacial syndromes, comorbidities affecting postsurgical healing, or those undergoing single-jaw surgery were excluded. Technical difficulty was defined by the presence of maxillary advancement >7 mm, maxillary segmentation, or posterior maxillary impaction >1.5 mm. Accuracy was measured as the root mean square linear discrepancy between planned and postoperative maxillary positions. Demographic characteristics and malocclusion type were recorded as covariates. Thirty-six patients were included, with a mean age of 27 years. Comparisons were made across advancement magnitude, segmentation status, and posterior impaction. No statistically significant differences in root mean square discrepancies were observed across landmarks or axes after correction for multiple comparisons, with the lowest observed probability value being 0.02. These findings demonstrate that PSI-assisted minimally invasive orthognathic surgery achieves clinically acceptable accuracy across varying levels of technical difficulty, supporting its reliable use even in technically demanding cases.

title: An unusual Case of p63/p40 Negative Myoepithelial cell-Rich Parotid Pleomorphic Adenoma.
abstract: Pleomorphic adenoma is the most common benign salivary gland neoplasm; however, myoepithelial-rich variants with unusual immunophenotypes are rare and pose diagnostic challenges. We report a myoepithelial-rich pleomorphic adenoma of the parotid gland in a 23-year-old male presenting with a slowly enlarging, painless infraauricular swelling. Grossly, the lesion was well-circumscribed and encapsulated. Histopathology revealed predominantly spindle, oval, and plasmacytoid myoepithelial cells embedded in densely hyalinized fibromyxoid stroma, with sparse ductal structures. The paucity of ducts and prominent myoepithelial proliferation closely mimicked myoepithelioma. Immunohistochemically, tumor cells showed diffuse expression of S100, pan-cytokeratin, and high-molecular-weight cytokeratin, supporting epithelial and myoepithelial differentiation. EMA and CD117 selectively highlighted the sparse ductal structures, providing a crucial diagnostic clue. Notably, the tumor was completely negative for p40, p63, and smooth muscle actin, representing an unusual immunophenotype for pleomorphic adenoma. Despite the absence of conventional myoepithelial markers, integration of the subtle residual ductal morphology and complementary immunoprofile established the diagnosis of myoepithelial-rich pleomorphic adenoma, excluding myoepithelioma and other salivary gland neoplasms. The patient recovered uneventfully after surgery and remained recurrence-free at six months. This case expands the immunohistochemical spectrum of pleomorphic adenoma and highlights that the absence of p40 and p63 expression should not preclude its diagnosis. Comprehensive immunohistochemical assessment, interpreted alongside meticulous histomorphological evaluation, is essential to avoid diagnostic pitfalls in these uncommon tumors.

title: Clinical T staging accuracy and its prognostic relevance in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Accurate clinical T-staging is essential for guiding surgical management in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), particularly when determining treatment escalation or de-escalation. This study evaluated its diagnostic accuracy and impact on potential over- and undertreatment. This retrospective single-center study included patients with histologically confirmed OSCC who underwent primary surgical resection with negative margins between 2012 and 2022. Clinical T-staging based on preoperative contrast-enhanced computed tomography and clinical examination was compared with pathological staging. The primary endpoint was the diagnostic accuracy of clinical T-staging, while secondary endpoints were overall survival and disease-free survival. A total of 637 patients were included in this study, from which 33.9% were inaccurately staged. Clinical stages T1 and T4a yielded the highest accuracy (81.6% and 84.1%), while stages T2 and T3 only had 69.2% and 64.3%. Midline tumors and patients with a clinically unsuspicious neck (cN0) were more frequently staged accurately. In survival analysis, inaccurate T-staging was not independently associated with worse overall survival (hazard ratio 0.91, 95% confidence interval 0.65-1.27, P = 0.59) or disease-free survival (1.02, 0.70-1.49, P = 0.93). Clinical T staging in OSCC was inaccurate in approximately one-third of cases, particularly in cT2-3 tumors, whereas cT1 and cT4a showed higher concordance. Although staging inaccuracies were not linked to survival, they may influence the extent of surgical resection and the overall invasiveness of the procedure.

title: Endoscopic transcanal repair of temporomandibular joint herniation into the external auditory canal: literature review.
abstract: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) herniation into the external auditory canal is a rare condition associated with anterior canal wall defects, most commonly due to a patent foramen of Huschke, trauma, or infection. The clinical presentation is variable and often non-specific, which may lead to misdiagnosis. High-resolution computed tomography is crucial for accurate diagnosis and effective surgical planning. While open surgical repair remains standard, minimally invasive approaches have not been widely reported. An 81-year-old male presented with right-sided otalgia exacerbated by mandibular movement and unresponsive to topical and oral antibiotics. He was initially diagnosed with malignant otitis externa. Otoscopic and radiological evaluations revealed a soft-tissue mass protruding through an anterior external auditory canal defect, consistent with TMJ herniation. After acute inflammation resolved, the patient underwent endoscopic transcanal surgical repair under general anaesthesia. The herniated TMJ capsule was dissected, and the osseous defect was reconstructed using layered autologous conchal cartilage and perichondrium. The procedure was completed entirely through the endoscopic approach without external incisions. At the 6-month follow-up, the patient remained asymptomatic, with complete graft integration and no recurrent herniation. Histopathological analysis excluded malignancy. This case illustrates the diagnostic challenge of TMJ herniation mimicking malignant otitis externa and demonstrates the feasibility of a fully endoscopic transcanal surgical approach for defect repair. The described minimally invasive technique offers a promising alternative to traditional open procedures, with reduced morbidity and favourable functional outcomes.

title: A Novel TCP and NTCP Modeling Framework Incorporating Inter-Fractional Deviations and Biological Effectiveness for Hyper-fractionated Radiotherapy.
abstract: Purpose High-dose hyper-fractionated radiotherapy has been recently included in NCCN guidelines for limited-stage small cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC), which clinical outcomes are dependent on actually delivered biologically effective dose (BED). However, most tumor control probability (TCP) and normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) models rely on planed physical dose without considering inter-fractional deviations and BED of fractionization. This study aims to develop TCP and NTCP models for LS-SCLC incorporating CBCT-based inter-fractional anatomies and hyper-fractional radiobiological dose. Methods and materials Inter-fractional dose was accumulated based on deformable image registration between CBCT and planning CT (pCT). Both TCP and NTCP were formulated within a BED-based framework, using dose-volume parameters calculated from planned dose and CBCT-based accumulated dose for comparison. The LQ model with "4R" effects and Gompertzian tumor growth (LQRG) and Lyman-Kutcher-Burman (LKB) models were used for TCP and NTCP modeling. Based on the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC), negative log-likelihood (NLL), and Akaike information criterion (AIC), model performances were assessed for local progression-free survival (LPFS), radiation pneumonitis and radiation esophagitis. Results Compared with pCT dose, CBCT dose showed superior discrimination of normal tissue toxicity. For grade ≥2 radiation pneumonitis, the CBCT-based NTCP model achieved significantly higher AUC (0.67 vs. 0.59) and lower NLL (62.39 vs. 66.13) than that of the pCT-based mode. Superiority of CBCT-based NTCP model was also observed for grade ≥3 radiation esophagitis, i.e., AUC (0.62 vs. 0.58) and NLL (55.55 vs. 56.64). Using the observed LPFS as reference, marginally improved TCP modeling was observed using CBCT dose than that of pCT, where the AUC values were 0.80 vs. 0.79 (GTV 45 Gy) and 0.77 vs. 0.75 (GTV 54 Gy). Conclusions By incorporating inter-fractional deviation and biological effectiveness, the improved accuracy of TCP and NTCP models provides preliminary evidence supporting the treatment planning and toxicity management for LS-SCLC patients treated with the hyper-fractionated radiotherapy, which needs further clinical validation.

title: PET-Guided Dose Escalation for Stage III Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: Purpose Uniform radiation dose escalation has not improved outcomes in locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and locoregional failure remains common despite multimodal therapy. We evaluated whether fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET)-guided dose escalation to metabolically active tumor subvolumes reduces locoregional failure compared with standard chemoradiation. Methods and materials PET-BOOST was a multi-institutional, open-label, phase 2 randomized trial conducted at 7 Canadian centers (January 2017-May 2022). Eligible patients had inoperable, FDG-avid stage IIIA/IIIB NSCLC and an achievable boost dose of at least 65 Gy. Patients were randomized 1:1 to standard chemoradiation with 60 Gy in 30 fractions or metabolically adaptive radiotherapy with an integrated boost to FDG-avid subvolumes to a maximum of 85 Gy in 30 fractions. Concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy was planned, and consolidation durvalumab was permitted after 2018. The primary endpoint was 2-year locoregional failure; secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), grade ≥3 treatment-related toxicity, and quality of life (QOL). Results Seventy-eight patients were randomized: 40 to standard radiotherapy and 38 to dose escalation, with a median follow-up of 5.0 years. Median age was 64.4 years; 53% were male, 62% had stage IIIA disease, and 76% received consolidation durvalumab. Median prescription boost dose was 75 Gy. Two-year locoregional failure was 27.5% with standard radiotherapy versus 18.4% with dose escalation (P=.13). Two-year OS (72.5% vs. 73.7%; P=.91) and PFS (52.5% vs. 57.9%; P=.74) did not differ between arms. Grade ≥3 treatment-related toxicities occurred in 25% versus 37% of patients (P=.26), with one grade 5 pulmonary hemorrhage in the dose-escalation arm. QOL did not differ between arms. Conclusions Metabolically adaptive PET-guided radiotherapy dose escalation was feasible in the context of consolidation immunotherapy and resulted in a numerically lower rate of locoregional failure, but did not significantly improve locoregional control or survival. The lower-than-anticipated event rate may have limited statistical power, and larger studies would be required to determine whether selective dose escalation provides a clinically meaningful improvement in locoregional control.

title: Implementing Image-Guided Brachytherapy (IGBT) For Cervical Cancer in Resource-Limited Settings: An International Multicentric Cross-Sectional Study of Resource and Workflow Impact.
abstract: Background Use of image-guided brachytherapy (IGBT) in cervical cancer improves patient outcomes. However, implementation in resource-limited settings is challenging due to limited capacity upscale, absence of workflow enhancement strategies, and financial barriers. Optimizing workflows is essential, yet the relationship between workflow efficiency and IGBT uptake remains unclear. Methods This cross-sectional study examined brachytherapy (BT) workflows across 14 nationally representative centers. Standardized forms collected data on infrastructure, treatment workflows ((A): Conventional two-dimensional (2D) X-Ray-Guided BT, with point-A-based fractions planned using 2D X-ray imaging, (B): Standard intracavitary (IC) three-dimensional (3D) IGBT, with fractions planned using computed tomography (CT)- or magnetic resonance (MR)-based imaging with volume-based prescriptions, (C): Advanced 3D IGBT, with fractions delivered using advanced IC or intracavitary-interstitial (IC-IS) techniques and planned using CT- or MR-based imaging with volume-based prescriptions.)), procedural times, anesthesia, imaging, and treatment planning. National BT resource data was also collected. Recommendations were developed to optimize workflows and facilitate IGBT transition. Findings A total of 365 workflows were analyzed, wherein workflow B was most common (51%). Median procedure times were 2 hours 08 minutes (Interquartile range (IQR) 1 hour and 7 minutes), 2 hours 35 minutes (IQR 1 hour and 51 minutes), and 4 hours 16 minutes (IQR 2 hours and 33 minutes) for workflows A, B, and C, respectively. Using sedation instead of full anesthesia shortened workflows by a median of 35 minutes. BT machine demand, based on national cervical cancer incidence, ranged from 0.2 to 9.5; four countries had low (< 0.5), two moderate (0.5 - 1.0), and eight high demand (>1.0). Resource- and context-specific recommendations for IGBT transition were provided. Interpretation BT workflows varied widely. Substantially increased procedure times and resource use were observed with advanced workflows. Findings highlight opportunities to improve efficiency through anesthesia choice, imaging strategy, and planning workflow optimization. Implementing context-specific strategies will be crucial for IGBT transition. Funding Funding from the XXXX, in collaboration with XXXX and participating sites.

title: Long-Term Outcomes of Lenalidomide-Dexamethasone in Combination With Radiotherapy in Solitary Plasmacytoma.
abstract: Introduction Radiotherapy achieves excellent local control in solitary plasmacytoma, but systemic progression remains a major limitation. We evaluated the long-term association between lenalidomide-dexamethasone combined with radiotherapy and disease outcomes. Materials and methods This retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained database included 75 consecutive patients with solitary plasmacytoma treated between 2004 and 2025. All patients underwent bone marrow assessment, serum free light-chain testing, and magnetic resonance imaging, with PET/CT routinely incorporated into staging from late 2008 onward. Patients received radiotherapy alone (n=42) or radiotherapy combined with lenalidomide-dexamethasone (n=33). Primary endpoints were progression-free survival and multiple myeloma-free survival. Systemic progression-free survival, defined by progression to multiple myeloma, multiple plasmacytomas, or distant solitary plasmacytoma, was additionally evaluated. Results Median follow-up was 6.31 years. Only three local recurrences occurred. Lenalidomide-dexamethasone was associated with longer progression-free survival (HR, 0.315; 95% CI, 0.128-0.775; p=0.012), with 10-year rates of 71.8% versus 26.7% after radiotherapy alone. Among the six patients progressing after combined treatment, three (50.0%) developed multiple myeloma and three (50.0%) developed multiple plasmacytomas. Multiple myeloma-free survival did not differ significantly between groups (10-year rates, 86.6% vs 65.9%; p=0.19). Conclusion Lenalidomide-dexamethasone combined with radiotherapy was associated with sustained improvement in progression-free survival in solitary plasmacytoma. These long-term findings support prospective evaluation of upfront lenalidomide-dexamethasone in combination with radiotherapy for solitary plasmacytoma.

title: Past, present and future of distal radius corrective osteotomy: From 2D based reconstruction to 3D data-driven, patient specific care.
abstract: Corrective osteotomy for distal radius malunion has evolved from two-dimensional (2D) radiograph based planning and surgeon performed geometric analysis to advanced three-dimensional (3D) virtual surgical planning (VSP). Historically guided by predefined radiographic parameters, contemporary practice increasingly emphasizes symptom severity and patient-specific functional goals. CT-based 3D models, contralateral surface matching, and patient-specific guides and implants have improved the accuracy of deformity correction. However, greater anatomical precision does not automatically translate into superior functional outcomes. Future progress depends on standardized evaluation frameworks, multicenter data collection, and predictive models to determine the clinical value of virtual surgical planning (VSP) and patient-specific implants (PSI) in delivering individualized, cost-effective and function-oriented care across the entire treatment pathway.

title: Can radiological parameters predict failure of fixation in distal radius fractures treated with a volar locking plate?
abstract: Introduction Fractures of the distal radius are common, and volar locking plates are the most utilized fixation method. Failure of fixation, defined as post-operative fracture collapse leading to loss of reduction and/or screw penetration, is an undesirable outcome. We aimed to demonstrate whether preoperative and intraoperative radiographic parameters are associated with subsequent failure of fixation in order to produce a model that may be able to predict failure. Methods A retrospective case-control study of 23 cases of failure of fixation matched to controls from the same cohort by age, sex, and AO classification in a 3:1 ratio. Nine initial injury and 13 intraoperative radiological parameters were evaluated, and multi-variate regression analysis models were analysed to assess if they could reliably predict failure. Results A total of 92 patients were analysed (23 cases, 69 controls). Size of intraarticular gap was the only preoperative parameter to be associated failure with every 0.47 mm increase in fracture gap resulting in a 1.6 increase of odds ratio of failure. Based on intraoperative radiological parameters, three factors were associated with failure: dorsal capitate translation, intraarticular gap and step. Models based on these parameters do not accurately predict failure, however, models based on intraoperative factors are associated with risk of failure with high specificity but low sensitivity. Conclusion We conclude that the severity of the injury is less importantly associated with failure of fixation, whereas the quality of the surgical fixation and specifically the accuracy of the reduction are more important.

title: Effect of AI-assisted radiographic fracture detection on paediatric emergency department length of stay through fracture exclusion: A before-after cohort study.
abstract: Background Artificial intelligence-assisted radiographic fracture detection tools (AI-RFDT) have the potential to support confident fracture exclusion by physicians in the paediatric emergency department (ED), where presentations for suspected fractures substantially outnumber confirmed fractures. This study aimed to evaluate whether implementation of AI-RFDT in a paediatric ED is associated with reduced length of stay (LOS) among patients presenting with suspected fractures, and to determine whether any observed effect is specifically mediated through the fracture-exclusion pathway. Patients and methods This retrospective before-after cohort study was conducted at a single tertiary paediatric ED. AI-RFDT (BoneView, Gleamer, Paris, France) was deployed on 1 October 2023 as a passive, second-read decision-support tool. The study population comprised 4172 paediatric patients with rule-out fracture diagnoses (fracture-excluded; F-E) during standard working hours (08:00-15:59; pre-AI n = 2514; post-AI n = 1658). Fracture-confirmed (F-C) patients served as a pre-specified internal control (n = 1155). The primary outcome was ED LOS; secondary outcomes were orthopaedic consultation rate, LOS by consultation status, anatomical subgroup LOS, and 30-day re-admission. Results Orthopaedic consultation rates in the paediatric ED decreased from 73% to 68.3% (Δ -4.7 %age points, p = 0.002). The greatest reduction was observed in patients discharged without orthopaedic consultation (2.25→1.78 h, Δ -28 min, p < 0.001), while those with confirmed fractures demonstrated no significant change in LOS (Δ+3 min, p = 0.51). 30-day re-admission rates remained unchanged (6.9% vs 6.9%, p = 1.00). Wrist and forearm injuries demonstrated the greatest LOS reduction (Δ -24 min, p = 0.004). Conclusions Deployment of AI-RFDT in a paediatric ED was associated with a reduction in LOS that was concentrated among patients discharged without orthopaedic consultation. The absence of LOS change in confirmed-fracture controls supports a mechanism specific to fracture exclusion rather than generalised care acceleration.

Wrist and forearm injuries demonstrated the greatest LOS reduction (Δ -24 min, p = 0.004).

Conclusions

Deployment of AI-RFDT in a paediatric ED was associated with a reduction in LOS that was concentrated among patients discharged without orthopaedic consultation. The absence of LOS change in confirmed-fracture controls supports a mechanism specific to fracture exclusion rather than generalised care acceleration.

title: Adjunct rim plating for selected pilon fracture patterns: Lessons from hyperextension tibial plateau fractures.
abstract: Background Pilon fractures frequently involve small anterior or anterolateral marginal fragments that are susceptible to shear displacement and may not be reliably controlled by conventional periarticular plates. Rim plating is a fragment-specific, low-profile juxta-articular buttress technique that has demonstrated favorable biomechanical and clinical results in selected tibial plateau fracture patterns. This review examines the rationale for extending this concept to selected pilon fracture patterns. Methods We performed a narrative review of clinical, cadaveric, and biomechanical studies describing rim-based constructs in tibial plateau fractures, with emphasis on hyperextension and posterolateral patterns, as well as computed tomography (CT)-based studies of pilon fracture morphology and fragment capture by precontoured plates. Relevant studies were identified through PubMed and reference screening and synthesized qualitatively to inform a technical proposal for adjunct rim plating in selected pilon fractures. Results The reviewed tibial plateau literature consistently identified peripheral regions that may remain unsupported by conventional periarticular plates, particularly in hyperextension and posterolateral fracture patterns, where adjunct rim plating has been associated with maintained reduction and favorable clinical outcomes. In the distal tibia, CT-based studies suggest that commonly used anatomically precontoured plates may not reliably capture the anterolateral (Tillaux-Chaput) fragment when fragment height is less than 15 mm. In this setting, an adjunct rim plate may serve as a peripheral buttress to improve support of the articular margin, distribute subchondral stress, and prevent displacement of the articular block. Conclusions Rim plating may be best conceptualized as a joint-line buttress strategy for improving peripheral containment of shear-dominant marginal fragments. Extrapolation of this concept to selected pilon fracture patterns is mechanically plausible and supported indirectly by CT-based fragment-capture data. This technique may be useful in carefully selected anterior or anterolateral distal tibial rim fractures that are not adequately controlled by standard periarticular plating.

title: Ischemic severity rather than ischemic time is associated with major limb complications in traumatic popliteal artery injury: A retrospective case series.
abstract: Purpose Although prolonged ischemic time is considered a key determinant of limb loss in traumatic popliteal artery injury (PAI), it does not fully explain the variability in clinical outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate whether ischemic severity at presentation is associated with major limb complications in PAI. Methods We retrospectively reviewed patients with blunt PAI treated at a single trauma center between 2013 and 2025. Ischemic severity was assessed using the Rutherford classification and the presence of collateral circulation on computed tomography angiography (CTA). Patients were categorized into mild ischemia (Rutherford grade I-II) and severe ischemia (Rutherford grade III). Outcomes included extensive soft tissue defects requiring reconstruction and amputation. Results Twenty-one limbs were included. Thirteen limbs were classified as mild ischemia and eight as severe ischemia. Collateral circulation was preserved in 17 limbs and absent in 4 limbs. The time to arterial reconstruction was comparable between groups. No major soft tissue complications occurred in the mild ischemia group. In contrast, 5 of 8 limbs with Rutherford grade III developed extensive soft tissue defects (p = 0.006). Absence of collateral circulation was also strongly associated with adverse outcomes, with all limbs without collateral flow developing major soft tissue complications (p = 0.002), despite a shorter time to revascularization. Conclusion Ischemic severity at presentation, particularly Rutherford grade III and absence of collateral circulation on CTA, is associated with major limb complications in traumatic PAI, whereas ischemic time alone may be insufficient to predict outcomes.

title: Advancing early detection of Alzheimer's disease: from established biomarkers to future innovations.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a major form of dementia, imposes an escalating global burden on public health and social care. Pathological changes in AD occur years before clinical symptoms, defining a prolonged preclinical phase. Currently, there is no effective treatment exist for late-stage AD, making early diagnosis and intervention indispensable, in which biomarkers play a pivotal role. While cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and positron emission tomography (PET) biomarkers improved AD diagnostic accuracy, their clinical application is limited by invasiveness, high costs. Advances in ultrasensitive immunoassay technologies has rendered peripheral blood biomarkers easily accessible, cost-effective, minimally invasive, and suitable for continuous monitoring, offering noval opportunities for AD screening, diagnosis and progression tracking. Additionally, non-invasive body fluids including saliva, urine and tears are being explored as potential biomarkers. Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven multimodal fusion, integrated with large-scale multimodal computing frameworks, significantly improve the accuracy of early AD diagnosis. Recent studies have identified a series of promising synaptic and neuronal biomarkers, such as neurofilament light chain (NFL), neurogranin (Ng), β-secretase 1 (BACE1) and synaptosomal-associated protein 25 (SNAP-25). Inflammatory mediators and genetic factors also contribute to AD pathological evaluation. This review systematically characterizes biomarker profiles of emerging non-invasive carriers (saliva, urine and tears). It further synthesizes cohort-derived quantitative diagnostic metrics (AUC, sensitivity, specificity) of multimodal AD biomarkers and conducts head-to-head comparison to clarify their respective strengths and translational limitations, aiming to provide evidence-based insights for optimizing early AD screening and diagnostic strategies.

title: Intelligent immunotherapy: AI-driven optimization of CAR-T therapy in hematologic malignancies.
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed outcomes in selected hematologic malignancies, yet its delivery remains constrained by variable efficacy, acute and prolonged toxicities, and complex manufacturing logistics. Artificial intelligence (AI) is being applied across the CAR-T continuum at three distinct levels of evidentiary maturity. Externally validated parsimonious models built on routine clinical and laboratory data including CAR-HEMATOTOX, endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) and m-EASIX, MyCARe, and gradient-boosting cytokine release syndrome predictors provide deployable risk stratification today. Methodologically sophisticated tools using deep-learning positron emission tomography (PET) segmentation, attention-based digital-pathology analysis, and multimodal fusion of imaging with laboratory and circulating tumor DNA features have demonstrated technical promise but generally lack the multi-center external validation required for clinical-grade deployment. Forward-looking applications, including digital-twin frameworks, large language models, and closed-loop adaptive therapy, remain at the prototype stage and have not yet been validated for CAR-T. This review synthesizes these three tiers, summarizes 18 published AI and statistical-modeling tools in a comparative performance table, and compares data characteristics and AI modeling paradigms across large B cell lymphoma, B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and multiple myeloma. We also identify the implementation realities-absent regulatory clearance, demographic and racial bias in training data, and post-deployment model drift-that condition the field's evolution. The contribution of AI to CAR-T therapy, as the evidence currently stands, is the calibrated quantification of established risk factors rather than the discovery of novel biology, but the methodological and data infrastructure foundations are now in place for the broader transformation that the next decade may enable.

title: Artificial intelligence across the gastric cancer care continuum: Clinical evidence, multimodal integration, and translation.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across the gastric cancer care continuum, but its clinical maturity differs substantially among endoscopy, cross-sectional imaging, digital pathology, prognostic modeling, treatment selection, and surgical support. Existing reviews have often focused on individual modalities or summarized algorithmic performance without systematically distinguishing technical feasibility from translational readiness. We conducted a structured narrative review of studies indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE and the Web of Science Core Collection from January 2022 through July 2026, supplemented by backward and forward citation tracking. Earlier landmark studies were retained when necessary to explain the development of major applications. Priority was given to prospective, multicenter, externally validated, and clinically actionable studies. Evidence maturity was assessed according to study design, validation breadth, workflow relevance, calibration and clinical-utility assessment, and implementation evidence. The main constraint on gastric cancer AI is no longer pattern-recognition capability but the absence of reproducible clinical benefit under real-world conditions. Priorities include multiregional prospective validation, standardized calibration and decision curve assessment, comparison of clinicians with and without AI, integration into existing workflows, evaluation of economic and patient-level outcomes, and post-deployment monitoring.

title: Habitat informed 3D deep learning predicts immunochemotherapy response in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Immunochemotherapy (ICT) is a critical treatment for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (LA-ESCC), yet predicting individual response remains challenging. We developed a three-channel 3D deep learning framework integrating tumor habitat analysis for predicting ICT response. In this multicenter retrospective study of 277 patients, voxel-level clustering of pretreatment CT images segmented tumors into habitat subregions reflecting microenvironmental heterogeneity. A ResNet-50 model incorporating habitat maps, cropped tumor images, and ROI masks achieved an AUC of 0.927 (95% CI, 0.850-0.951) in the independent external test cohort, compared with 0.869 for habitat radiomics (DeLong p = 0.343). SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified texture features, particularly gray-level co-occurrence matrix correlation in habitat 3, as the primary contributors. This framework provides a noninvasive approach for predicting ICT response in LA-ESCC.

title: Assessing the incidence of retinal hemorrhage in pediatric patients following COVID-19 vaccination.
abstract: Background Retinal hemorrhages (RHs) are a cardinal finding in abusive head trauma (AHT) for which a broad differential diagnosis is appropriate to consider. The frequency of COVID-19 vaccination and reports of subsequent ocular manifestations have led to the consideration of whether COVID-19 vaccination should be included in the RH differential. This study aimed to investigate the frequency of RH following COVID-19 vaccination in children. Methods In this single-center, retrospective, observational cohort study, we reviewed the medical records of children ≤8 years of age who received a COVID-19 vaccine from July 1, 2020, to July 1, 2024, and underwent a fundus examination within 21 days of vaccination. The main outcome measure was incidence and characteristics of RH on fundus examination. Results Of 17,926 children vaccinated during this period, 203 subjects met inclusion criteria and underwent 212 unique examinations, with mean age of 4.56 years (0-8) at the time of first examination. Twenty examinations were also in the setting of prior COVID-19 infection. No examinations revealed RH. Based on Hanley's rule of zero incidence, the 95th percentile upper limit of incidence of RH after COVID-19 vaccination is 4.11% at 7 days, 2.04% at 14 days, and 1.42% at 21 days following vaccination. Conclusions RHs were not seen in any children within 21 days of COVID-19 vaccination. This suggests that RH is rare following COVID-19 vaccination and perhaps of little relevance to the differential diagnosis of RH in the evaluation for AHT.

title: Intraoperative and radiographic indicators of extraocular muscle aberrancy in syndromic craniosynostosis.
abstract: Background Strabismus is common in syndromic craniosynostosis, often attributed to abnormal extraocular muscle (EOM) trajectory, and orbital anatomy. Absent EOMs have been reported, but the spectrum of primary dysgenesis remains poorly understood. The purpose of this study was to characterize the range of EOM dysgenesis in a large cohort that had undergone strabismus surgery. Methods The medical records of patients with syndromic craniosynostosis treated at Boston Children's Hospital (2010-2023) were reviewed retrospectively to identify all cases with neuroimaging and history of strabismus surgery. Genetic testing results and EOM abnormalities noted on neuroimaging or during surgery were recorded. Imaging was reviewed to determine presence of each EOM. Superior oblique muscle (SO) size was classified as "normal" if its transverse diameter was at least one-half that of the adjacent medial rectus muscle. Results A total of 47 patients with syndromic craniosynostosis had undergone strabismus surgery, of whom 43 had available neuroimaging. Syndromic associations were as follows: 21 patients with Apert, 10 with Crouzon, 6 with Pfeiffer, 5 with Saethre-Chotzen, and 1 with Muenke. Rectus and inferior oblique muscles were universally present. SO size was normal in only 15 of 86 eyes (17%). EOM aberrancies were noted intraoperatively in 15 of 43 operative cases (35%), including diaphanous insertions, bifid or fused rectus muscles, and posterior inferior oblique insertions. Results of genetic testing were available for 26 patients, 24 of whom had FGFR2 mutations, including all 10 (of 15) patients with intraoperatively noted EOM aberrancies who underwent genetic testing. Conclusions In this cohort with syndromic craniosynostosis, thin-section or high-resolution orbital imaging demonstrated presence of all rectus muscles even when insertions were diaphanous. The SO was hypoplastic in 83%. Aberrancies noted intraoperatively in 35% likely underestimate the true incidence, because evaluation was limited to muscles targeted for surgery.

title: A Knowledge Graph Framework for Longitudinal Congenital Heart Disease Modeling: Methodology Corner.
abstract: Background Congenital heart disease (CHD) is characterized by evolving clinical trajectories; staged interventions; and complex relationships among diagnoses, procedures, and encounters. Conventional machine learning applied to electronic health record (EHR) data often rely on static feature representations that do not preserve the natural longitudinal disease progression or clinical context. Objectives The purpose of this study was to develop a knowledge graph-based framework for trajectory-aware representation and analysis of longitudinal CHD EHR data. Methods We constructed a longitudinal knowledge graph that integrates patients, encounters, diagnoses, and procedures while preserving temporal ordering across the care continuum. Term frequency-inverse document frequency and Word2Vec approaches were applied to encounter contexts extracted from the graph to generate longitudinal patient representations that supported phenotyping, patient similarity analysis, and retrospective classification. Results Using accumulated longitudinal EHR from a cardiovascular magnetic resonance cohort, we demonstrate that the framework captured clinically meaningful patterns and supported retrospective identification of single ventricle physiology as a representative use case. Conclusions This knowledge graph framework provides a scalable approach for preserving temporal and relational clinical context and enable trajectory-aware modeling of longitudinal cardiovascular EHR data in patients with CHD.

This knowledge graph framework provides a scalable approach for preserving temporal and relational clinical context and enable trajectory-aware modeling of longitudinal cardiovascular EHR data in patients with CHD.

title: Absence of Fibrosis Influences Prognosis of Cardiac Resynchronization in Nonischemic Cardiomyopathy: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background In patients with nonischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) undergoing cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT), there are no clear recommendations on selecting CRT with defibrillator (CRT-D) vs pacemaker (CRT-P). Patients with high probability of response to CRT and low arrhythmic risk may be ideal candidates to CRT-P. Objectives The objectives of the study was to evaluate if the absence of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is associated with CRT response and ventricular arrhythmia (VA) in NICM treated with CRT. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted. Search of PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus identified observational studies of NICM patients who underwent cardiac magnetic resonance before CRT implantation. Studies assessing echocardiographic response to CRT or VA stratified by LGE status were included. The VA endpoint comprised sustained ventricular tachycardia, appropriate implantable cardioverter-defibrillator therapy, resuscitated cardiac arrest, and sudden death. Results Ten studies were included: 9 (n = 831) for CRT response and 6 (745 patients) for arrhythmic risk. CRT response was significantly higher in patients without LGE than in patients with LGE (78.7% vs 50.7%; P < 0.001). The cumulative incidence of VA was extremely low in LGE cases, significantly lower than that of LGE+ ones (0.8% vs 21.1%, P < 0.001). The absence of LGE was strongly associated with higher CRT response (OR: 3.52; 95% CI: 2.54-4.88; P < 0.001) and much lower arrhythmic risk (OR: 0.06; 95% CI: 0.02-0.15; P < 0.001). Conclusions In NICM patients undergoing CRT, the absence of LGE is strongly associated with greater echocardiographic response and very low arrhythmic risk. In this subgroup the incremental benefit of CRT with defibrillator over CRT-P may be limited.

title: Artificial Intelligence Detection of Aortic Valve Calcification on Routine Noncontrast Chest CT: A Real-World Cohort.
abstract: Background Routine noncontrast chest computed tomography (CT) may reveal aortic valve calcification (AVC) outside aortic stenosis evaluation. Its prevalence, burden, and documentation remain uncertain. Artificial intelligence (AI) may enable systematic detection. Objectives The study aims to evaluate AVC prevalence and burden, clinical correlates, radiology documentation, and AI-assisted case finding. Methods This retrospective single-center study screened 511 consecutive noncontrast, non-electrocardiographically gated chest CT examinations in adults aged ≥50 years. After 15 protocol exclusions and 56 software-designated nonevaluable examinations, 440 underwent quantification by 2 blinded readers. AVC was defined as >10 AU using a 130-Hounsfield-unit threshold adjusted for blood-pool attenuation and image noise when needed. Locked HealthAVC V1.0 was a secondary comparator. Results Manual quantification identified AVC in 172 of 440 scans (39.1%; 95% CI: 34.6%-43.7%); 97 of 440 (22.0%) had ≥100 AU. Inter-reader agreement at >10 AU was 99.5% (kappa = 0.990). Age (adjusted OR: 1.92 per 5 years; 95% CI: 1.63-2.26) and male sex (adjusted OR: 2.09; 95% CI: 1.32-3.30) were associated with AVC. Reports documented 27 of 172 positive scans (15.7%; 95% CI: 11.0%-21.9%). AI detected 169 of 172 manually confirmed cases (98.3%) among 440 evaluable scans, including 142 of 145 undocumented cases. Of 496 submitted scans, 56 (11.3%) were nonevaluable. End-to-end sensitivity counting positive rejected scans as missed was 89.9%. Among 86 AI-positive patients with echocardiography, 10 (11.6%) had mild-or-greater aortic stenosis. Conclusions AVC was common but infrequently documented on routine chest CT. AI detected most cases among evaluable scans; 11.3% were nonevaluable, yielding 89.9% end-to-end sensitivity. Prospective studies should assess clinical pathways.

title: Endovascular Solution for Anastomotic Pseudoaneurysm of the Ascending Aorta.
abstract: Objective The objective was to demonstrate the feasibility of ascending thoracic endovascular aortic repair (a-TEVAR) as a minimally invasive treatment for an ascending anastomotic pseudoaneurysm in a patient unsuitable for redo open surgery. Key steps The steps included: 1) multidisciplinary evaluation and detailed computed tomography angiography-based anatomical planning; 2) assessment of proximal and distal landing zones, coronary ostia, and supra-aortic vessel anatomy; 3) selection of a Gore C-TAG endograft based on anatomical suitability; 4) percutaneous transfemoral a-TEVAR under rapid ventricular pacing with intraoperative angiographic guidance; and 5) confirmation of complete pseudoaneurysm exclusion while preserving coronary and supra-aortic vessel patency, followed by serial computed tomography angiography surveillance. Potential pitfalls Limited landing zones, proximity to the coronary ostia and supra-aortic vessels, inaccurate device deployment, and the absence of dedicated ascending aortic devices increase procedural complexity. Careful patient selection, meticulous preoperative planning, and rapid ventricular pacing are essential to minimize these risks. Take-home messages The a-TEVAR procedure is a feasible alternative to high-risk redo sternotomy in carefully selected patients with favorable anatomy. However, a-TEVAR of the ascending aorta continues to pose significant technical and clinical challenges, and further investigations are needed.

title: Extremely Severe Aortic Stenosis Mimicking Cardiac Amyloidosis on Multimodality Imaging.
abstract: Cardiac amyloidosis is increasingly recognized in older patients with severe aortic stenosis, yet advanced pressure-overload remodeling can produce overlapping imaging features that confound noninvasive diagnosis. A 70-year-old woman presented with progressive exertional dyspnea and markedly elevated cardiac biomarkers. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed extremely severe calcific aortic stenosis, increased left ventricular wall thickness, and severely reduced global longitudinal strain. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated elevated native T1 and extracellular volume with late gadolinium enhancement, and cardiac amyloid radionuclide imaging showed Perugini grade 1 uptake. Despite clinical suspicion of cardiac amyloidosis, noninvasive findings remained inconclusive. The patient underwent surgical aortic valve replacement with intraoperative myocardial biopsy, which demonstrated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and interstitial fibrosis without amyloid deposition, consistent with advanced pressure-overload remodeling rather than infiltrative disease. Extremely severe aortic stenosis can mimic cardiac amyloidosis across multiple imaging modalities. Histologic confirmation remains essential when noninvasive findings are discordant or inconclusive. Severe aortic stenosis may closely mimic cardiac amyloidosis on multimodality imaging. Histological confirmation can be decisive in resolving diagnostic uncertainty.

title: PCCT and IVUS-NIRS for High-Risk Plaque Management.
abstract: Background High-risk coronary plaque may be underrecognized in patients with atypical symptoms and negative biomarkers. Advanced coronary imaging can add anatomical and prognostic information. Case summary A 59-year-old woman presented with acute chest pain, mild ischemic electrocardiographic changes, and negative high-sensitivity troponin. Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) showed a predominantly noncalcified, lipid-rich-appearing plaque in the left anterior descending artery despite a low risk profile. Angiography confirmed significant stenosis, and intravascular ultrasound with near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) demonstrated a high-risk plaque phenotype with maximum lipid core burden index over 4 mm of 347. Percutaneous coronary intervention used distal drug-coated balloon treatment and proximal-to-mid drug-eluting stent implantation. Postprocedural imaging confirmed adequate stent expansion and lower NIRS lipid signal. Discussion This case highlights the complementary role of PCCT and intravascular imaging for identifying and managing vulnerable coronary plaque. Take-home message PCCT for noninvasive plaque characterization and intravascular ultrasound-NIRS for intraprocedural guidance provide a complementary strategy for personalized management of vulnerable coronary plaque.

title: Giant Aneurysm of a Classic Blalock-Taussig Shunt in Adult Tetralogy of Fallot.
abstract: Background Giant aneurysmal degeneration of a classic Blalock-Taussig (BT) shunt is a rare, life-threatening late complication of tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) palliation. Case A 47-year-old woman with unrepaired TOF palliated in childhood presented with exertional dyspnea and a right thoracic mass. Echocardiography revealed severe right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, a large ventricular septal defect, and a pulsatile extracardiac structure. Computed tomography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging confirmed a giant (72 × 66 mm) true aneurysm of a right BT shunt. She underwent successful aneurysm excision, ventricular septal defect closure, right ventricular outflow tract reconstruction, and pulmonary valve replacement. Discussion This case demonstrates a rare late complication of a classic BT shunt decades after TOF palliation. Conclusion Classic BT shunts may develop life-threatening aneurysmal degeneration decades after palliation, emphasizing lifelong surveillance and timely definitive management. Take-home message Lifelong imaging surveillance and multimodality imaging are essential for detecting late vascular complications.

title: Durable Vessel Patency Achieved by Drug-Coated Balloon-Only Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Triglyceride Deposit Cardiomyovasculopathy.
abstract: Background Triglyceride deposit cardiomyovasculopathy (TGCV) causes triglyceride accumulation in cardiomyocytes and vascular smooth muscle cells, leading to diffuse coronary artery disease and frequent restenosis after percutaneous coronary intervention. Case summary A 37-year-old man with diabetes mellitus presented with diffuse 3-vessel coronary disease. Angiography and computed tomography revealed concentric diffuse coronary stenoses, and intravascular ultrasound demonstrated periadventitial low-echoic structures. Iodine-123-β-methyl-iodophenyl pentadecanoic acid scintigraphy showed a severely reduced washout rate, supporting the diagnosis of TGCV. The patient underwent percutaneous coronary intervention using a cutting balloon followed by drug-coated balloon angioplasty without stent implantation. No restenosis was observed by angiography at 1 year or computed tomography at 3 years. Discussion This case suggests that a stentless revascularization strategy using a drug-coated balloon may be a feasible option in TGCV, potentially avoiding pathological vascular responses associated with permanent metallic scaffolds. Take-home message Stentless intervention may represent a promising therapeutic option in patients with TGCV.

title: Cardiac CT Planning of Surgical Treatment of Multiple Coronary-Pulmonary Fistulas With Chronic Coronary Occlusion.
abstract: Anatomy Coronary fistulas are rare congenital anomalies that may lead to myocardial ischemia through a coronary steal phenomenon, particularly when associated with coronary artery disease. Pathology We describe a case of cardiac computed tomography angiography (CCTA) diagnosis of multiple coronary-pulmonary artery fistulas associated with chronic occlusion of the right coronary artery, in a 66-year-old man presenting with unstable angina. Imaging correlation CCTA and echocardiography were used for evaluation of procedural planning in an acute setting. Treatment The fistulas were effectively treated with surgical exclusion combined with coronary artery bypass grafting, yielding an optimal result on the postoperative computed tomography scan. Take-home messages Coronary fistulas are rare but important causes of myocardial ischemia. This case highlights the importance of CCTA definition of anatomical complexity and multidisciplinary decision-making in the management of complex coronary fistulas. Surgical repair remains the preferred approach in complex anatomy cases or associated coronary artery disease requiring revascularization.

This case highlights the importance of CCTA definition of anatomical complexity and multidisciplinary decision-making in the management of complex coronary fistulas. Surgical repair remains the preferred approach in complex anatomy cases or associated coronary artery disease requiring revascularization.

title: Multisource Coronary Artery Fistula Draining Into the Coronary Sinus: Multimodality Imaging and Surgical Repair.
abstract: Background Coronary artery fistula (CAF) is a rare congenital coronary anomaly. Multisource CAF draining into the coronary sinus is exceptionally uncommon and anatomically complex. Case presentation A woman presented with progressive exertional dyspnea and right-sided heart failure. Multimodality imaging, including transthoracic echocardiography, coronary computed tomography angiography, and invasive coronary angiography, demonstrated multisource CAFs arising from the right coronary artery and left circumflex artery draining into the coronary sinus with diffuse aneurysmal coronary dilatation. The patient underwent surgical ligation of the dominant right CAF with concomitant tricuspid annuloplasty. Postoperative imaging demonstrated successful closure of the dominant right CAF with thrombus formation within the ligated fistulous tract, whereas the smaller left circumflex artery fistula persisted, and serial follow-up demonstrated clinical improvement. Conclusion Multimodality imaging is essential for diagnosis, treatment planning, and postoperative surveillance of complex CAF. Surgical repair remains an effective treatment strategy for anatomically complex fistulas associated with significant hemodynamic consequences.

title: Electrical Storm in Advanced Chagas Cardiomyopathy Treated With Stereotactic Arrhythmia Radiotherapy After LVAD Implantation.
abstract: Background Refractory ventricular tachycardia (VT) in advanced Chagas cardiomyopathy remains challenging after prior ablation and mechanical circulatory support. Case summary A 40-year-old man with advanced Chagas cardiomyopathy and prior endo-epicardial VT ablation developed electrical storm during influenza A infection and underwent left ventricular assist device implantation as a bridge to transplantation. Despite unloading, antiarrhythmic therapy, overdrive pacing, and stellate ganglion modulation, monomorphic VT persisted. Repeat ablation was unfavorable because of frailty and extensive residual lateral scar. Targeting for stereotactic arrhythmia radiotherapy (STAR) integrated late gadolinium enhancement cardiac magnetic resonance, clinical VT morphology, prior electroanatomic mapping, and planning computed tomography. A single 25-Gy fraction was delivered without acute complications. No sustained VT or implantable cardioverter-defibrillator shocks occurred during follow-up. Discussion Multimodality-guided STAR was feasible in this critically ill left ventricular assist device-supported patient. Although stabilization cannot be attributed to STAR alone, radiotherapy was delivered without observed acute radiotherapy- or device-related complications. Take-home message STAR may offer a noninvasive substrate-targeted option when repeat ablation is limited.

title: Early Diagnosis, Delayed Treatment, and Fulminant Progression of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Associated Myocarditis.
abstract: Background Prompt immunosuppressive therapy is recommended for immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis; however, the optimal timing in asymptomatic patients remains uncertain. Case summary A woman in her 60s receiving adjuvant pembrolizumab for melanoma developed asymptomatic cardiac troponin I (cTnI) elevation (93 pg/mL) before her ninth cycle. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging met diagnostic criteria for myocarditis; however, immunosuppressive therapy was withheld because of the absence of symptoms and mild cTnI elevation. One week later, she developed symptomatic myocarditis with a marked cTnI increase (4,115 pg/mL), requiring intensive care, corticosteroid pulse therapy, and temporary mechanical circulatory support. Discussion This case demonstrates that asymptomatic immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis can progress rapidly despite seemingly low initial risk, underscoring the importance of ongoing risk assessment following diagnosis. Take-home messages Early diagnosis alone may not be sufficient to prevent disease progression. Risk stratification and timely intervention during the presymptomatic phase may improve patient outcomes.

title: Lipoprotein-insulin resistance score is associated with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease in liver transplant recipients.
abstract: Background Liver transplant (LT) recipients have increased atherogenic risk, which is difficult to quantify via available diagnostic tests. Objective The aim of the present study was to evaluate the diagnostic performance of the lipoprotein insulin resistance index (LP-IR) score, a composite biomarker of insulin resistance and metabolic risk, and its association with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) in LT recipients. Methods Analysis was performed in 218 LT recipients who were enrolled in a natural history study. Blood samples were collected after an overnight fast, and LP-IR was analyzed via nuclear magnetic resonance. The primary outcome was a composite endpoint consisting of new-onset coronary artery disease, nonfatal myocardial infarction, stroke, or sudden cardiac death. Cox regression models were constructed and adjusted to traditional ASCVD risk factors, liver disease, and immunosuppression. Results ASCVD was present in 47 LT recipients after a median follow-up of 47 months after study enrollment. In the adjusted analysis, LP-IR was significantly associated with future risk of the primary outcome, with a hazard ratio of 1.024 (95% CI 1.009 and 1.039, P = .002) that was independent of conventional risk factors. Combining LP-IR with diabetes improved the performance compared to either parameter alone. LP-IR had a higher diagnostic performance compared to the conventional lipid profile (low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, total cholesterol) and hepatic panel in predicting future risk of ASCVD. Conclusion LP-IR is associated with future risk of ASCVD in LT recipients with or without diabetes and may have utility as a prognostic biomarker; however, study findings require development of a risk model and further validation.

title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria® Pretreatment Evaluation and Follow-Up of Endometrial Cancer: 2026 Update.
abstract: Endometrial cancer is the most common gynecologic malignancy in the United States, and accurate pretreatment evaluation is essential for risk stratification, treatment planning, and detection of recurrent disease. This evidence-based review summarizes imaging recommendations for patients with established endometrial cancer undergoing pretreatment assessment, surveillance, or evaluation for suspected recurrence. MRI pelvis without and with intravenous contrast is usually appropriate for assessment of local tumor extension across histologic subtypes and grades. For aggressive histologic tumor types, or when metastatic disease is suspected, CT chest, abdomen, and pelvis with intravenous contrast and FDG-PET/CT are usually appropriate for evaluation of nodal and distant metastases. Routine imaging surveillance is usually not appropriate for asymptomatic patients with treated low- or intermediate-risk disease, whereas CT may be appropriate in selected asymptomatic high-risk patients. MRI pelvis, CT chest, abdomen, and pelvis, and FDG-PET/CT are usually appropriate for suspected recurrence. The American College of Radiology Appropriateness Criteria are evidence-based guidelines for specific clinical conditions that are reviewed annually by a multidisciplinary expert panel. The guideline development and revision process support the systematic analysis of the medical literature from peer reviewed journals. Established methodology principles such as Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation or GRADE are adapted to evaluate the evidence. The RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method User Manual provides the methodology to determine the appropriateness of imaging and treatment procedures for specific clinical scenarios. In those instances where peer reviewed literature is lacking or equivocal, experts may be the primary evidentiary source available to formulate a recommendation.
