title: Msx1 orchestrates retinal progenitor cell homeostasis from mechanical locking to synthetic arrest through the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway.
abstract: Despite the known association between the muscle segment homeobox 1 (Msx1) gene and neural diseases, its function in maintaining homeostasis in adult retinal progenitor cells (RPCs) unclear. We using an in vitro adult RPC model combined with short hairpin RNA-mediated knockdown, RNA sequencing, and tandem mass tag -based proteomics define Msx1 as a homeostatic rheostat that orchestrates cell structural dynamics and metabolic signaling pathways. We demonstrate that Msx1 loss triggers a mechanical locking state, defined by a paradoxical uncoupling of actomyosin dynamics: elevated Myh14 coexists with global attenuation of stability factors (Cnn1, Mad2l1b), causing aberrant punctate aggregation of Rho-GTPases and arresting cell movement, with subsequent metabolic paralysis through suppression PI3K/AKT signaling and induction of G2/M cell cycle arrest. Ultimately, these events converge toward synthetic arrest by the transcriptional translational decoupling of ribosomal protein large subunit hubs. These results indicate a severe blockade of de novo protein synthesis. Our findings indicate that Msx1 knockdown not only inhibit cell cycle progression but also disrupt the homeostatic rheostat, causing RPCs to undergo irreversible fate failure via a cascade of mechanical, metabolic, and synthetic failures. This regulatory model offers new insights into retinal regeneration, suggesting that therapeutic restoration of cytoskeletal and translational homeostasis may be required to re-establish the remodeling competence of retinal progenitor cells in degenerative retinal diseases.

title: Baseline MRI markers and clinical outcomes during anti-amyloid β therapy: A real-world study in a Japanese dementia center.
abstract: Importance Predictors of decline and of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) during anti-amyloid β therapy in routine care are undefined. Objective To identify baseline predictors of cognitive, functional, and safety outcomes. Design, setting, and participants Retrospective cohort of 161 consecutive patients initiating anti-amyloid β therapy at a Tokyo dementia center, 2024 to 2026 (lecanemab, 89; donanemab, 72). Exposures Lecanemab or donanemab. Main outcomes and measures Change in MMSE and CDR-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB); baseline medial temporal atrophy (VSRAD Z score), amyloid PET burden, and microbleeds; ARIA. Results With lecanemab, MMSE and CDR-SB declined significantly at every assessment (CDR-SB +0.79, +1.10, +1.60 at 6, 12, 18 months); memory and orientation declined while language was preserved. Greater baseline medial temporal atrophy was associated with greater 12-month CDR-SB worsening (r = 0.39; P = .01; n = 40); patients in the most severe standard category (Z ≥ 3) worsened by 2.62 versus 0.64 points (adjusted β = +2.18; P < .001). Atrophy was associated with older age (r = 0.19; P = .03) and with baseline memory-related measures - ADAS-Cog score (r = 0.32; P < .001) and the MMSE subdomains of delayed recall (β = -0.25; P = .006) and time orientation (β = -0.30; P = .04) - but not MMSE total score. Amyloid PET burden showed no significant association at most time points. All ARIA events were asymptomatic; ARIA-H occurred in 6 of 25 with microbleeds versus 3 of 136 without (odds ratio, 14.0; P < .001). Donanemab follow-up was 6 months. Conclusions and relevance Baseline medial temporal atrophy was associated with functional decline and microbleeds with ARIA-H. Pretreatment MRI may provide prognostic and safety information during anti-amyloid β therapy.

title: A dual-tower multimodal framework with feature quality enhancement for predicting pathological complete response after neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer: a multicenter study.
abstract: Background Pathological complete response (pCR) is a key endpoint following neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in breast cancer, with potential to guide treatment adaptation and surgical de-escalation. However, limited generalizability across institutions remains a major challenge due to heterogeneous imaging protocols (scanner vendors, field strengths, and acquisition parameters) and diverse patient populations, which can cause significant domain shifts in model performance. This study develops and externally validates a multimodal framework for post-neoadjuvant, preoperative prediction of pCR using multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) and routinely available clinical data. Methods In a multicenter retrospective setting, 1291 patients from five institutions were enrolled and institutionally divided into a development cohort pooled from two centers (n=683) and three independent, single-center external validation cohorts (n=608). Model inputs comprised post-treatment mpMRI (dynamic contrast-enhanced and diffusion-weighted imaging) for deep feature extraction, clinicopathological variables, radiomics features from both pre- and post-treatment scans, and delta-radiomics features capturing longitudinal within-sequence changes (Δ = post - pre). A dual-tower attention network incorporating a Feature Quality Enhancer (FQE) module-which regularizes the latent space by promoting intra-class compactness, inter-class separability, and feature consistency-was designed to learn discriminative imaging representations. Deep, radiomic, and clinical features were then integrated through a hierarchical feature selection strategy, with robustness assessed via repeated experiments.. Predictive performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) in both development and external validation cohorts. Results The proposed AIFPS achieved an AUC of 0.882 (95% CI: 0.855-0.905) in the development cohort. In external validation, AIFPS achieved the highest numerical AUCs (0.853, 0.888, and 0.895) and demonstrated statistically significant improvements over all single-modality models in all cohorts. While its superiority over certain dual-modality models did not reach statistical significance after correction for multiple comparisons, the full multimodal approach consistently yielded the numerically highest discrimination. Conclusion AIFPS integrates quality-enhanced deep imaging features with radiomics, including delta-radiomics, and clinicopathological variables to enable accurate and generalizable preoperative prediction of pathological complete response, particularly in HER2-positive disease, while further validation is required for triple-negative and luminal subtypes. Its application in luminal breast cancer requires further dedicated subtype-specific modeling. With prospective validation, this approach may support individualized treatment stratification following neoadjuvant chemotherapy.

title: Integrative single-cell and computational pathology analyses reveal a C11orf24-associated stem-like epithelial population linked to tumor microenvironment remodeling and immune evasion in bladder cancer.
abstract: Background Cancer stem-like cells drive tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, yet the epithelial stemness hierarchy in bladder cancer (BLCA) remains poorly defined. We aimed to characterize stemness-associated epithelial populations and their clinical significance. Methods We analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing data from 92,218 cells across 13 treatment-naïve BLCA samples to characterize epithelial stemness and tumor-microenvironment interactions. Spatial transcriptomics and independent bulk cohorts were used for orthogonal and clinical validation. An HStem-associated histopathology-based prognostic model was developed by integrating quantitative image features with deep-learning representations, followed by functional validation of the candidate gene C11orf24. Results We identified a highly stem-like epithelial population (HStem) at the apex of the differentiation hierarchy, exhibiting MYC activation, oxidative phosphorylation, and DNA repair enrichment, with preferential presence in advanced-stage tumors. HStem cells were inferred to serve as major communication hubs within the TME, interacting extensively with fibroblasts and endothelial cells via MIF-CD74/CXCR4 and MIF-CD74/CD44 axes. An 86-gene HStem signature enabled development of a robust image-based prognostic model. High-risk tumors showed immune exclusion, immunosuppressive enrichment, T-cell dysfunction, and predicted checkpoint blockade resistance. C11orf24 emerged as a candidate stemness-associated regulator; C11orf24-positive cells displayed enhanced stemness and stromal interactions. Functional experiments demonstrated that C11orf24 perturbation altered clonogenic growth, migration, and invasion in BLCA cells. Pharmacogenomic analyses identified predicted therapeutic vulnerabilities that warrant experimental validation. Conclusions We identify an HStem population associated with BLCA progression, microenvironmental remodeling, and immune evasion. Integrating single-cell and spatial transcriptomics with computational pathology, we establish a clinically relevant stemness framework and identify C11orf24 as a potential therapeutic target, offering opportunities for stemness-directed precision oncology.

title: Regional Expansion of Transplant Oncology: The First Case of Liver Transplantation for Unresectable Colorectal Liver Metastasis in the Gulf Region.
abstract: Introduction Liver transplantation for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) has emerged as a potential curative option for highly selected patients with unresectable liver-only disease, with recent trials demonstrating 5-year overall survival rates of 55% to 83%. Surgical resection remains the only curative treatment for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM), but its applicability is limited, with only 25% of patients eligible. However, this approach remains investigational with limited global experience and has never been implemented in the Middle East region. Recently, liver transplantation (LT) has emerged as a potential curative option for select patients with unresectable liver-only metastases. This report highlights the potential for liver transplantation to serve as a curative modality in highly selected patients with CRLM and demonstrates its feasibility in a new geographic region. Case report We report the first case in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region of a 41-year-old male with unresectable CRLM who underwent LT following an aggressive multimodal pretransplant protocol. The patient was initially treated at an outside facility for synchronous left-sided colorectal cancer with liver metastases, achieving complete remission after FOLFOX chemotherapy. He subsequently developed 2 liver recurrences: the first in July 2023, with 17 metastases managed at the outside facility by surgical resection and chemotherapy; and the second in October 2023, with 40 metastases, treated with systemic chemotherapy and trans arterial radioembolization (TARE-Y90). He received additional treatment with ablative liver-directed therapies consistent with the "Cleveland Protocol." The patient subsequently underwent orthotopic liver transplantation. His postoperative course was complicated with moderate acute cellular rejection, which was successfully treated, and he was discharged on post-operative day 16. Conclusion This case demonstrates the successful implementation of liver transplantation for CRLM in the Gulf region, achieving disease-free survival at 4-month follow-up despite high-risk biological features typically associated with poor prognosis. It illustrates the feasibility and potential benefit of LT for unresectable CRLM in carefully selected patients, following an aggressive pretransplant locoregional therapy protocol modeled after the Cleveland Clinic approach. Key success factors included rigorous patient selection using established criteria (Oslo score 0, low Fong score, low PET-MTV), intensive pretransplant optimization with multimodal therapy, and experienced multidisciplinary management of post-transplant complications. With careful patient selection and integration of systemic and liver-directed therapies to achieve maximal disease control, this strategy may help expand transplant eligibility, possibly offering a curative approach. This case provides valuable regional data for the evolving role of transplant oncology in colorectal cancer management in a resource-limited setting.

title: Incidentally Diagnosed Pulmonary Embolism Two Months After Living Liver Donation in a Donor With Homozygous MTHFR A1298C Mutation: A Case Report.
abstract: Living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) is widely performed in countries with limited cadaveric organ donation. Although donor hepatectomy is generally safe, venous thromboembolic events such as pulmonary embolism (PE) remain rare but potentially life-threatening complications. Genetic thrombophilia, including methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) mutations, may contribute to thrombotic risk. A 39-year-old female living liver donor underwent right donor hepatectomy for LDLT. The donor had no preoperative risk factors for venous thromboembolism, and a routine thrombophilia panel, including protein C, protein S, antithrombin III, factor V Leiden, and prothrombin gene mutations, was normal. Two months after surgery, an abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan performed due to fluid collection adjacent to the remnant liver in ultrasound (USG) during routine follow-up incidentally revealed partial PE. Pulmonary CT angiography confirmed the finding, while lower extremity Doppler USG showed no evidence of deep vein thrombosis. Laboratory tests revealed elevated D-dimer and homocysteine levels. Further genetic evaluation demonstrated a homozygous MTHFR A1298C mutation. The patient was treated with low molecular weight heparin followed by oral anticoagulant therapy for 6 months, resulting in complete radiological resolution of the embolism. PE after donor hepatectomy is rare but potentially fatal. This case suggests that MTHFR A1298C mutation may represent a previously underrecognized risk factor for venous thromboembolism in living liver donors. In populations with a high prevalence of MTHFR mutations, extended thrombophilia screening and appropriate thromboprophylaxis may help reduce the risk of postoperative thromboembolic complications.

title: Rapid Progression of Cardiac Allograft Vasculopathy With Sudden Cardiac Death Within the First Year of Heart Transplantation: A Case Report.
abstract: Cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV) is a major cause of mortality and morbidity within the first 3 years of heart transplantation (HT). CAV results in progressive coronary artery stenosis and may lead to arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. In some cases, sudden cardiac death represents the initial presentation of CAV, as cardiac denervation blunts anginal symptoms that otherwise could have preceded sudden cardiac death (SCD). Here, we describe the case of a 56-year-old man with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy. He underwent left ventricular assist device implantation followed by orthotopic HT. Five months after transplantation, he presented with atypical mid-sternal chest discomfort initially thought to be musculoskeletal in origin. Routine coronary angiography at 12 months revealed severe, diffuse 3-vessel disease consistent with International Society of Heart and Lung Transplantation (ISHLT) CAV-3, and cardiac MRI revealed full thickness delayed enhancement in the inferior wall consistent with infarction. Despite overall preserved left ventricular ejection fraction, he developed polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT) with an appropriate shock from a wearable cardioverter-defibrillator (WCD) and was transferred with an intra-aortic balloon pump to a larger transplant center and underwent another heart transplantation. This case highlights rapid CAV progression leading to infarction and arrhythmia despite preserved LVEF, emphasizing the need for enhanced screening with biomarkers and imaging as well as earlier consideration for device-based strategies to prevent sudden cardiac death in high-risk transplant recipients.

title: Inadvertent Coronary Sinus Cannulation During Central Venous Catheter Placement in a Liver Transplant Recipient with Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava: A Case Report.
abstract: Persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC) is the most common thoracic venous anomaly and is usually asymptomatic. Central venous catheterization through a PLSVC can be challenging, and inadvertent advancement of catheters into the coronary sinus may result in arrhythmias, perforation, thrombosis, or inaccurate hemodynamic measurements. We report a case of coronary sinus cannulation by a left internal jugular dialysis catheter in a liver transplant recipient with previously unrecognized PLSVC. Initial chest radiography suggested catheter termination within a duplicated left superior vena cava; however, intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) demonstrated the catheter tip within the coronary sinus. The catheter was withdrawn under direct echocardiographic guidance, avoiding potential complications. This case highlights the utility of intraoperative TEE for definitive localization of central venous catheters in patients with anomalous thoracic venous anatomy.

title: MRI-visible CDDO-Me@AL/HA hydrogel for theranostics of radiation-induced intestinal injury.
abstract: Radiation-induced intestinal injury (RIII) is a serious complication of abdominal and pelvic radiotherapy. Its mechanism is complex, and traditional treatment methods are difficult to achieve precise intervention and efficacy visualization. Bardoxolone methyl (CDDO-Me) has a therapeutic effect on intestinal injury as an Nrf2 activator. However, there are limitations such as uncontrolled drug release and lack of efficacy visualization. To address this problem, we prepared a sodium alginate/hyaluronic acid (AL/HA) pH-responsive oral hydrogel loaded with CDDO-Me, and introduced melanin nanoparticles (SMNP) with enhanced MRI signal to achieve non-invasive visualization of the distribution, localization and retention of the hydrogel in rats. The hydrogel exhibited resistance to gastric acid, mucoadhesive properties, and prolonged retention in the small intestine and colon, thus achieving controlled intestinal release of drugs. In addition, our research suggested that the oral CDDO-Me@AL/HA@SMNP hydrogel could alleviate intestinal oxidative stress injury and down-regulate pro-inflammatory cytokines in mouse models. These effects may be associated with Nrf2 activation and ROS clearance, and may also involve the PI3K/Akt/GSK3β pathway. Overall, our research indicated that the CDDO-Me@AL/HA@SMNP hydrogel integrates therapeutic efficacy with MRI-based visualization/tracking capabilities for RIII. These findings represent a preclinical proof-of-concept, and further optimization, safety evaluation, and translational studies are required before any potential clinical application.

title: Evaluation of nanofibrillated cellulose as a urethral bulking agent in female dogs with acquired urethral sphincter mechanism incompetence: a prospective clinical study.
abstract: Urethral bulking agent (UBA) implantation is a minimally invasive, effective and safe alternative treatment for refractory urethral sphincter mechanism incompetence (USMI). However, repeated implantations are frequently needed to maintain continence. Therefore, a prospective interventional clinical study with eight client-owned neutered female dogs was designed to evaluate the clinical efficacy and 12-month outcome of nanofibrillated cellulose (NFC), a novel biomaterial as a UBA. Concurrent causes of urinary incontinence were excluded with clinical and neurological assessment, blood and urine sampling, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), retrograde vaginourethrography, cystoscopy, and urodynamic testing. A continence score (CS) was assigned before and after treatment, and monthly thereafter. Furthermore, the dogs were followed with MRI, retrograde vaginouretrography, and urethroscopy at 1 and 12 months or at the time of euthanasia or recurrence. All dogs were continent (CS ≥ 8/10) at 1 month with a significant increase in mean CS (p < 0.0001, difference 5.4, 95% CI 4.1-6.6). Median duration of continence was 8 months (IQR 4 - not estimable). At 12 months, the treatment response was still significant (p = 0.0010) with (n = 4/7) or without (n = 3/7) medical intervention. The imaging and urethroscopy findings suggest that flattening of the deposits with or without mucosal ulceration may contribute to recurrence. Sporadic bacterial cystitis was diagnosed in two dogs and recurrent cystitis in one. In conclusion, NFC showed promising short-term effect and a low complication rate when used as a UBA. Urinary incontinence resolved after single NFC implantation in all dogs for a median of 8 months without adjunctive treatment.

title: Sheep pulmonary image recognition (SPIRO): An explainable deep learning framework for macroscopic assessment of ovine pulmonary lesions.
abstract: Accurate detection and classification of pulmonary diseases in sheep are critical for ensuring animal welfare, food safety, and effective disease surveillance in abattoir settings. In this study, we propose a two-stage, explainable, histopathology-informed deep learning framework for the automated classification of ovine lung lesions. The dataset comprises 1052 sheep lung images, annotated through a dual-level diagnostic process involving macroscopic inspection and histopathological confirmation, and classified as healthy, inflammatory, or neoplastic. Four convolutional neural network architectures-VGG16, VGG19, ResNet50, and EfficientNetB0-were benchmarked under identical conditions. EfficientNetB0 achieved the highest observed standalone performance and was integrated into a two-stage pipeline, in which YOLOv11 first localized lung regions and EfficientNetB0 subsequently classified the cropped images. Model interpretability was evaluated using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM). The YOLOv11-EfficientNetB0 pipeline achieved an overall test accuracy of 90% and a weighted F1-score of 0.88. Neoplastic lesions were classified with the highest performance, reaching precision, recall, and F1-score values of 0.98, 0.99, and 0.99, respectively, while healthy and inflammatory lungs achieved F1-scores of 0.83 and 0.82, respectively. Grad-CAM visualizations indicated that predictions were mainly driven by diagnostically relevant pulmonary regions. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of explainable artificial intelligence for objective, scalable, and biologically grounded post-mortem assessment of sheep lungs, with potential applications in abattoir surveillance, veterinary pathology, and flock health monitoring.

title: Improving shear-wave speed analysis in penile vibro-ultrasound elastography using self-supervised deep learning-based IQ denoising.
abstract: Objective Ultrasound vibro-elastography (UVE) estimates tissue stiffness from externally induced shear waves. In cylindrical structures such as the penis, reflections and multidirectional interference produce complex wavefields that reduce acquisition reliability. The purpose of this research is to develop a deep learning-based framework to improve shear-wave speed (SWS) analysis. Methods A deep learning (3D U-Net) IQ-denoising framework is proposed to suppress reflected, interfering, and non-propagating wavefield components prior to physics-based inversion. The framework processes measured IQ wavefields and reconstructs SWS using the local phase velocity imaging with wave-based filtering (LPVI-WBF) algorithm. A two-stage quality-control pipeline classifies acquisitions as Good, Borderline, or Bad using thresholds τ_keep = 0.45 and τ_rel = 0.33. The network is trained on Cohort A (10 patients, 342 acquisitions) via self-supervised Noise2Self and evaluated on an independent Cohort B (6 patients, 902 acquisitions) and a simulation cohort (n = 90). Results On Cohort B, deep learning (DL) rescued 376/403 Borderline acquisitions (93.3%) and preserved 89.4% of native-Good, raising the Pass rate from 38.7% to 91.8% (+53.1%). Rescued and native-Good SWS distributions were statistically indistinguishable: independent comparison (n = 227 vs 376) yielded δ = ±0.099 m/s (TOST p < 0.0001), and 198 matched pairs confirmed δ = ±0.161 m/s - both well below the ± 0.30 m/s clinical margin. In simulation, Borderline-acquisition reliability rose from 0.239 to 0.503 (n = 35; Δ = +0.264, p < 0.0001), with paired SWS equivalence at a ± 0.50 m/s margin. Conclusion Self-supervised deep learning-based IQ denoising acts as a reliability reconstructor for processing SWS data, expanding the acquisition population usable for physics-based inversion while leaving the physics-based LPVI-WBF inversion itself unchanged.

title: Automated Segmentation of Intrinsic Foot Muscles in Ultrasound Using Deep Neural Networks: Development and Validation Study.
abstract: Objective To develop and validate the first automated deep-learning image-processing framework for pixel-level segmentation of the plantar intrinsic foot muscles (PIMs) in ultrasound (US) images. This approach supports objective and reproducible US-based muscle segmentation from conventional B-mode images. Methods US images of four PIMs (abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis (FDB), quadratus plantae [QP] and abductor digiti minimi) were collected from 200 healthy participants (n = 1099 images). Manual segmentations were used as ground truth. Three deep neural network architectures (U-Net, Feature Pyramid Network [FPN] and DeepLabV3+) with a Mix Transformer backbone were trained and evaluated. Model performance was assessed using the Intersection over Union (IoU) and Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), two complementary pixel-level segmentation metrics. Agreement with manual measurements was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), mean difference and standard error of measurement. Results All models demonstrated excellent segmentation performance, with mean IoU values ≥0.90 and mean DSC values ≥0.95 across all muscles. The highest accuracy was observed for the FDB (IoU = 0.95; DSC = 0.97), while QP showed slightly lower performance (IoU = 0.90; DSC = 0.95). FPN and DeepLabV3+ exhibited greater stability (SD: ±0.02-0.03) compared to U-Net (up to ±0.08). Agreement with manual segmentation was high for cross-sectional area (ICC: 0.836-0.960) and moderate-to-high for border length (ICC: 0.705-0.944), with minimal systematic bias. Mean model inference time was under 0.01 s per image, reflecting forward-pass model inference only and excluding image loading, resizing and post-processing. Conclusion This study presents the first automated segmentation framework for the PIMs in US. Built on established segmentation architectures with a Mix Transformer backbone, it enables accurate and reliable pixel-level segmentation in under 0.01 s per image; its novelty lies in extending automated musculoskeletal US analysis to this previously unaddressed muscle group. By automating tissue boundary detection at the pixel level, this framework advances US imaging beyond conventional manual measurement, enabling objective and scalable musculoskeletal assessment with reduced operator dependence at the segmentation stage. These findings establish the feasibility of accurate and reproducible PIM segmentation in healthy adults and provide the necessary foundation for subsequent validation in clinical populations.

title: Deep Learning-Enabled Automated B-mode Segmentation for Regional Cerebral Perfusion Assessment in Neonates Using Ultrafast Power Doppler.
abstract: Cerebral perfusion disturbances contribute to neonatal brain injury, and ultrafast power Doppler can quantify regional cerebral blood volume but relies on manual segmentation that limits clinical use. We developed and validated a U-Net model for automated regional brain segmentation on B-mode images derived from neonatal transfontanellar ultrafast ultrasound to enable rapid arterial and venous cerebral blood volume quantification. Time-integrated, log-compressed ultrafast B-mode images from 80 neonates were manually segmented by an expert into the cortico-sub-cortical areas, the cingulate gyrus and the basal ganglia, and then used to train a U-Net with class-weighted loss (a 70/15/15 train/validation/test split). The trained model was then applied to segment B-mode images, with the resulting regions of interest used to quantify arterial and venous cerebral blood volume from the corresponding power Doppler data. Segmentation performance was quantified using the Dice similarity coefficient, with agreement between artificial intelligence- and manually derived cerebral blood volume assessed by Bland-Altman analysis. The median Dice similarity coefficients were 83%, 84% and 88% for the three regions. Mean Bland-Altman differences were ≤0.103 dB (arterial) and ≤0.096 dB (venous). Perturbation of the predicted masks by ±35% surface area change showed the narrowest limits of agreement at the unperturbed prediction, changing by no more than 0.1 dB between -5% and +5%, demonstrating automated segmentation as a rapid, reproducible alternative to manual delineation.

title: Automated Quantification of 3-D Carotid Ultrasound Vessel Wall Texture Change Predicts Vascular Events.
abstract: Objective To reduce reliance on labor-intensive and operator-dependent explicit plaque segmentation, we evaluated whether a texture-change score (ΔTexture) derived from semi-automated 3-D ultrasound (3-DUS) vessel wall segmentation predicts vascular events better than baseline vessel wall texture (BL-Texture), vessel wall volume change (ΔVWV) and Framingham risk score. Methods 3-DUS images were acquired from 272 patients with carotid atherosclerosis at baseline and 1 y later. Vessel walls were delineated using a validated, minimally user-initialized segmentation workflow. Longitudinal texture change was summarized as vessel wall ΔTexture and compared with BL-Texture, ΔVWV and Framingham risk score. Patients were followed for up to 5 y (median, 3.16 y) for myocardial infarction, transient ischemic attack and stroke. Results ΔTexture and BL-Texture predicted vascular events (log-rank, p < 0.001 for both), whereas ΔVWV did not. No event occurred in the lowest-risk tertile of ΔTexture. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of ΔTexture was 0.89, compared with 0.82 for BL-Texture, 0.53 for ΔVWV and 0.53 for Framingham risk score. In Cox regression, ΔTexture (median hazard ratio, 4.05; p < 0.001) and BL-Texture (median hazard ratio, 3.63; p < 0.001) were significant predictors, whereas ΔVWV and Framingham risk score were not. Conclusion Vessel wall ΔTexture derived from minimally user-initialized 3-DUS vessel wall segmentation predicted vascular events better than ΔVWV and Framingham risk score. This approach provides a scalable imaging biomarker for vascular event risk assessment without requiring explicit plaque segmentation.

title: Doppler-based Radiomics Integrated With Frozen Section Analysis Enhances Borderline Ovarian Tumor Prediction: A Multicenter Study.
abstract: Objective To develop a Doppler-based radiomics model that utilizes tumor characteristics related to neovascularization, with or without integrating intraoperative frozen section analysis (FSA), to enhance borderline ovarian tumors (BOT) prediction. Methods In this retrospective multicenter study, patients diagnosed with BOT or epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) between January 2010 and October 2022 across five centers were included. Data from Center I were randomly divided into training (80%) and validation (20%) sets, while Centers II-V provided the test set. Three ultrasound-radiomics models were developed: color Doppler features (CD), grayscale features (GS), and combining both (GSCD). An Integration Model was developed by incorporating clinical variables, FSA and the best-performing radiomics model. Color Doppler signals were acquired through three channels with RGB information. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results A total of 1244 patients with a median age of 49 years (IQR, 37-58 years) were included, consisting of 520 patients with BOT and 724 EOC. The GSCD exhibited the best predictive performance for BOT among the three ultrasound-radiomics models, showing an AUC of 0.975 (95%CI, 0.962-0.985) in the training set, with a sensitivity of 92.9% and a specificity of 88.9% in the validation set. The Integration Model further improved the performance, achieving an AUC of 0.997 (95%CI, 0.993-0.998) in the training set, with a sensitivity of 87.2% and a specificity of 98.7% in the validation set. Additionally, both the GSCD and Integration Model effectively distinguished BOT from Stage I EOC, with AUCs of 0.919 (95% CI: 0.849-0.963) and 0.936 (95% CI: 0.871-0.974) in the validation set. Conclusion We developed a Doppler-based radiomics model utilizing red-green-blue information. This model, irrespective of integration with FSA, demonstrated improved accuracy in predicting BOT and stratified the FIGO Stage EOC.

title: Deep Learning-Driven Multimodal Integration of Ultrasound and CT for Identifying Central Lymph Node Metastasis in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the utility of multimodal imaging biomarkers in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), this study developed a deep learning model using ultrasound (US) and computed tomography (CT) imaging to predict central lymph node metastasis (CLNM) in PTC by integrating radiomic features of perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) at the cervical vertebra 6 (C6) level. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 477 PTC patients from two centers. Using ResNet101 with Hierarchical Attention Integration (ResHAI-101), we extracted deep learning features of the tumor area from US images. Separately, we extracted radiomic features of PVAT from CT images. Univariate and multivariate analyses were conducted based on clinical data, followed by feature selection and integration. Results Multimodal prediction model performance was quantified by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Predictive performance was validated using an external test cohort (ETC). The Multimodal Prediction Model 3, integrating deep learning features, PVAT radiomic features and clinical features, showed superior diagnostic performance for predicting CLNM compared to the Unimodal Model, achieving AUCs of 0.915 in the internal test cohort and 0.890 in the ETC. Binary logistic regression identified gender, age, tumor size and extrathyroidal extension as independent risk factors for CLNM. Conclusion This study establishes and validates the significant impact of PVAT on CLNM in PTC, providing a non-invasive tool for pre-operative risk assessment to aid in surgical decision-making.

title: Ultrasound Localization Microscopy Combined With Regional Division for Differentiating Benign and Metastatic Lymph Nodes.
abstract: Objective Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (ULM) enables high-resolution visualization of lymph node microvasculature. However, most previous studies rely on whole-node analysis, which may overlook spatial heterogeneity and be affected by confounding factors. This prospective single-center study aimed to investigate the diagnostic value of ULM combined with regional analysis for differentiating benign and metastatic lymph nodes. Methods A total of 104 lymph nodes from patients with sonographically suspicious lymph nodes were included. All lymph nodes underwent ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy, which served as the reference standard for classification (benign or metastatic). Each lymph node was divided into central, peripheral, and global regions, and ULM quantitative parameters were extracted. Regional ratio features were calculated. Feature selection was performed using univariate analysis, LASSO regression, and backward stepwise logistic regression. Model performance was evaluated using 10-fold stratified cross-validation, 2000 bootstrap resamples, decision curve analysis (DCA), and clinical impact curve (CIC). Results Three diagnostic models were constructed: a conventional ultrasound (US) model, a ULM model, and a combined US-ULM model. The combined model demonstrated the best discriminative performance with an AUC of 0.866 (95% CI: 0.7875-0.9320), followed by the ULM model (AUC = 0.833, 95% CI: 0.7464-0.9108) and the US model (AUC = 0.730, 95% CI: 0.6219-0.8285). In multivariable analysis, SD.Density_C_P (OR =0.0578, p = 0.012), FD_C_P (OR = 0.8847 per 0.01 increase, p = 0.003), and peripheral vascular pattern (OR = 10.9501, p < 0.001) were identified as significant predictors of lymph node metastasis. At optimal cut-off values, the combined model achieved a sensitivity of 0.733 and specificity of 0.915. Conclusion The proposed region-based ULM model combined with conventional ultrasound provides an improved quantitative approach for differentiating benign and metastatic lymph nodes in patients with sonographically suspicious lymphadenopathy.

title: Ultrasound Localization Microscopy as a Novel Imaging Technique for Differentiating Autoimmune Pancreatitis From Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: A Preliminary Prospective Study.
abstract: Objective Focal autoimmune pancreatitis (AIP) mimics pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) radiologically, posing diagnostic challenges. This exploratory study investigated ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) for quantitative microvascular characterization and compared its diagnostic performance with that of conventional contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS). Methods In this prospective exploratory study, 30 patients with solid pancreatic lesions, including 15 with AIP and 15 with PDAC, underwent conventional ultrasound and CEUS followed by offline ULM reconstruction from arterial-phase raw RF data. Qualitative CEUS features and quantitative time-intensity curve parameters were assessed. Quantitative ULM parameters were extracted from lesion and matched perilesional pancreatic ROIs, and derived heterogeneity metrics were calculated. Histological vascular area fraction was quantified for correlation analysis. The diagnostic performances of CEUS and ULM parameters were evaluated and compared using receiver operating characteristic analysis with bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals. Results ULM showed significantly greater vascular density and more homogeneous intralesional vascular distribution in AIP than in PDAC (both p < 0.001). AIP also exhibited higher vessel ratio, perfusion index, fractal number, mean velocity, and mean diameter. Among the ULM parameters, the Δ fractal number and normalized fractal number showed the highest diagnostic performance, both achieving an AUC of 0.985. By comparison, the best-performing individual CEUS feature, enhancement intensity, yielded an AUC of 0.800, while its combination with washout pattern increased the AUC to 0.867. Among the quantitative CEUS parameters, half-intensity time and mean transit time performed best with AUCs of 0.880 and 0.864, respectively. ULM vessel ratio showed a significant positive correlation with histological vascular area fraction. Conclusion As a preliminary exploration, ULM demonstrated feasibility for characterizing microvascular differences and yielded higher diagnostic accuracy than CEUS parameters in a selected cohort. These findings require validation in larger, multicenter studies before ULM can be considered as a clinical biomarker for this differential diagnosis.

title: Endorectal Ultrasound-Based Habitat Analysis for Pathologic Response Prediction After Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer.
abstract: Objective To investigate the value of endorectal ultrasound (ERUS)-based habitat analysis in predicting pathologic response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NCT) in locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC). Methods Consecutive patients treated between January 2018 and May 2025 were randomly divided into training and test sets at a 7:3 ratio. Tumor habitat subregions were defined using K-means clustering, and radiomic features were extracted and selected. Clinical, habitat, and fusion models were developed, and model performance was evaluated using ROC analysis, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Among 407 patients, tumor location, cT stage, extramural vascular invasion, and tumor-stroma ratio differed significantly between good- and poor-response groups (p < 0.05). For predicting response to NCT, the clinical, habitat, and fusion models achieved AUCs of 0.885 (95% CI: 0.840-0.927), 0.911 (95% CI: 0.872-0.943), and 0.958 (95% CI: 0.935-0.979) in the training set and 0.757 (95% CI: 0.668-0.841), 0.720 (95% CI: 0.599-0.828), and 0.829 (95% CI: 0.737-0.906) in the test set, respectively. In the test set, the fusion model outperformed the habitat model (p = 0.010), whereas the difference from the clinical model was not statistically significant (p = 0.097). The fusion model exhibited the highest sensitivity in both sets (0.956 and 0.897, respectively). In the test set, it yielded the lowest Brier score (0.174) and generally provided the greatest net benefit across most threshold probabilities of 0.12 to 0.75. Conclusion The fusion model demonstrated promising performance for predicting response to NCT in LARC. Prospective multicenter external validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Preclinical Studies of MVT-100, A Novel Ultrasound Enhancing Agent.
abstract: Objective Over the past decades, many investigations have used perfluorocarbon (PFC)-based contrast products to enhance ultrasound (US) imaging. Currently octafluoropropane (OFP), decafluorobutane, and sulfur hexafluoride or a combination of those gases is used for the preparation of ultrasound enhancing agents (UEA). This study reports the development of MVT-100, a novel microbubble ultrasound enhancing agent (UEA) designed for improved stability, safety, and imaging performance. The objective of these studies was to fully characterize and compare the biophysical, chemical and in vivo properties of the new UEA (herein referred to as MVT-100) as compared with the well-known and widely utilized UEA known as perflutren lipid microspheres (Perflutren) (commercialized under the name of Definity®). Methods Analytical methods were used to characterize the MBs. Low mechanical index (MI) contrast-enhanced ultrasound was performed in mice and pigs. Results Comparison of Perflutren MB with MVT-100 MB showed similarities of the products in their overall particle numbers, gas content, osmolality, pH and phospholipid concentrations. However, MVT-100 exhibited a zeta potential that was essentially neutral (+0.5 ± 0.1 mV), compared with the negative zeta potential of Perflutren (-4.2 ± 2.0 mV), a tighter size distribution and lower polydispersity index (0.114 ± 0.012 vs. 0.159 ± 0.036, p = 0.048). Under accelerated storage conditions (40°C for 4 weeks), MVT-100 demonstrated markedly greater lipid stability, with only 2.05% loss of total phospholipid content compared with 13.10% for Perflutren. Murine renal retention studies showed that MVT-100 MB exhibited significantly lower (∼2.5 fold) renal retention in the kidney as compared with Perflutren. In porcine studies, MVT-100 hemodynamic parameters were identical to those of Perflutren. Echocardiographic porcine studies showed that ventricular opacification and endocardial border delineation following MVT-100 administration were comparable between agents at early time points, with higher and more sustained opacification with MVT-100 at later time points (generalized linear mixed model: main effect of agent p < 0.001, time × agent interaction p < 0.001) and no evidence of a significant difference in acoustic shadowing between agents (p > 0.99). Conclusions MVT-100 is a novel UEA that exhibits promising properties as a new imaging agent for contrast echocardiography with appealing storage conditions.

Objective

Over the past decades, many investigations have used perfluorocarbon (PFC)-based contrast products to enhance ultrasound (US) imaging. Currently octafluoropropane (OFP), decafluorobutane, and sulfur hexafluoride or a combination of those gases is used for the preparation of ultrasound enhancing agents (UEA). This study reports the development of MVT-100, a novel microbubble ultrasound enhancing agent (UEA) designed for improved stability, safety, and imaging performance. The objective of these studies was to fully characterize and compare the biophysical, chemical and in vivo properties of the new UEA (herein referred to as MVT-100) as compared with the well-known and widely utilized UEA known as perflutren lipid microspheres (Perflutren) (commercialized under the name of Definity®).

Methods

Analytical methods were used to characterize the MBs. Low mechanical index (MI) contrast-enhanced ultrasound was performed in mice and pigs.

Results

Comparison of Perflutren MB with MVT-100 MB showed similarities of the products in their overall particle numbers, gas content, osmolality, pH and phospholipid concentrations. However, MVT-100 exhibited a zeta potential that was essentially neutral (+0.5 ± 0.1 mV), compared with the negative zeta potential of Perflutren (-4.2 ± 2.0 mV), a tighter size distribution and lower polydispersity index (0.114 ± 0.012 vs. 0.159 ± 0.036, p = 0.048). Under accelerated storage conditions (40°C for 4 weeks), MVT-100 demonstrated markedly greater lipid stability, with only 2.05% loss of total phospholipid content compared with 13.10% for Perflutren. Murine renal retention studies showed that MVT-100 MB exhibited significantly lower (∼2.5 fold) renal retention in the kidney as compared with Perflutren. In porcine studies, MVT-100 hemodynamic parameters were identical to those of Perflutren. Echocardiographic porcine studies showed that ventricular opacification and endocardial border delineation following MVT-100 administration were comparable between agents at early time points, with higher and more sustained opacification with MVT-100 at later time points (generalized linear mixed model: main effect of agent p < 0.001, time × agent interaction p < 0.001) and no evidence of a significant difference in acoustic shadowing between agents (p > 0.99).

Conclusions

MVT-100 is a novel UEA that exhibits promising properties as a new imaging agent for contrast echocardiography with appealing storage conditions.

title: An Exploratory Study of Fusion of Intratumoral and Peritumoral Ultrasound Radiomics With Clinical Features for Distinguishing Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma From Hodgkin Lymphoma.
abstract: Objectives To develop a model integrating clinical features with intratumoral and peritumoral ultrasound radiomics features for distinguishing Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) from Hodgkin Lymphoma (HL). Methods This study retrospectively analyzed data from 102 DLBCL patients (218 enlarged lymph nodes) and 37 HL patients (105 enlarged lymph nodes) at The First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University. The enlarged lymph nodes were randomly allocated to a training cohort (227 nodes) and a test cohort (96 nodes) in a 7:3 ratio. Radiomics models were constructed based on ultrasound images from both the primary tumor and the peritumoral regions (8/16/24-pixel extensions). For the optimally performing regions of interest, two fusion strategies, a feature-based and a decision-based model, were applied to build the fusion models. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves, with the area under the curve (AUC) calculated to quantify discriminative ability. Clinical utility was assessed through decision curve analysis (DCA). Calibration curves were generated to evaluate the goodness-of-fit. The study strictly adhered to the TRIPOD-AI checklist. Results In the test cohort, the radiomics model using a 16-pixel peritumoral extension demonstrated optimal performance with an AUC of 0.636. The decision-based fusion model (Radexpand16_Clinica_R) achieved the highest AUC (0.943) among all models evaluated. Additionally, the Radexpand16_Clinica_R model exhibited excellent sensitivity, specificity, and favorable clinical utility as shown by DCA. Conclusions Our exploratory analysis suggests that a decision-based fusion model shows potential in differentiating DLBCL from HL. Incorporating peritumoral regions improved the predictive capability of the radiomics models.

title: Research Progress of Low-Intensity Pulsed Ultrasound in Parkinson's Disease.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder where current pharmacological and surgical interventions, including Deep Brain Stimulation, often fail to reverse neuronal degeneration or halt disease progression. Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) has emerged as a novel, non-invasive neuromodulation technology with significant therapeutic potential. This review synthesizes current research on the key acoustic parameters, biological mechanisms, and clinical applications of LIPUS in PD. Unlike High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU), which relies on thermal ablation to destroy target nuclei (e.g., Vim, STN), LIPUS utilizes low-energy mechanical waves (typically <3 W/cm²) to exert non-thermal regulatory effects without damaging tissue. Mechanisms of action include the modulation of mechanosensitive ion channels (e.g., Piezo1), enhancement of neuroplasticity via brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), promotion of autophagy, and regulation of microglial phenotypes to reduce neuroinflammation. We further compare LIPUS with HIFU, highlighting the superiority of LIPUS regarding safety, reversibility, and the absence of requirement for MRI-based thermal monitoring. While preliminary clinical studies using wearable LIPUS devices indicate improvements in motor and cognitive functions, a unified consensus on optimal stimulation parameters and targeting strategies is lacking. Future research should focus on large-scale, standardized clinical trials to establish precise protocols for LIPUS as a disease-modifying therapy for PD.

title: Perilesional biopsy in - systematic out? Comparative analysis of targeted, perilesional and systematic core yield by needle tracking with robotic-assisted transperineal MRI/US fusion prostate biopsy.
abstract: Objectives To characterize prostate cancer (Pca) detection rates by Gleason Grade Group (GG) in targeted, perilesional, and systematic cores sampling the remaining prostate using robotic-assisted transperineal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) /ultrasound fusion biopsy (RA-TP-FBx), enabling precise spatial documentation of every core relative to MRI-lesions and the prostate. Methods We analyzed prospectively collected RA-TP-FBx cases between 2020 and 2024. Biopsies were performed with the iSR'obot Mona Lisa (Biobot). Sampling included a traditional targeted + systematic strategy and a Trizonal approach: targeted + perilesional + systematic. Perilesional cores were defined at biopsy as samples within 10 mm of the MRI-lesion margin and systematic cores as samples outside the targeted-perilesional areas. Individualized 3D prostate maps were correlated with per-core histopathology. Clinically significant PCa (csPCa) was defined as GG ≥ 2. Results The full cohort included 566 RA-TP-FBx cases. Diagnosis of csPCa (n=131 in the Trizonal cohort) was exclusively due to perilesional sampling in 6.1% (8/131). Systematic biopsy detected csPCa not captured by targeted or perilesional cores in 3.8% (5/131), but only 1.5% (2/131) originated from MRI-negative lobes. Overdetection of GG 1 (n = 58 in the Trizonal cohort) would be reduced by 24.1% (14/58) by omitting systematic cores when targeted and perilesional cores were negative. Conclusions Robotic-assisted mapping demonstrated that perilesional sampling effectively complemented targeted biopsy, while systematic cores yielded minimal additional csPCa detection but increased GG 1 overdetection. These data support adopting targeted + perilesional sampling and omitting or deintensifying the routine addition of systematic cores in the remaining prostate.

title: Integrated molecular, immunological, oxidative stress, and histopathological evaluation of Ascaridia galli infection in chickens.
abstract: Ascaridia galli (A. galli) is an important intestinal nematode of chickens, but the host immune, oxidative, and pathological responses associated with natural infection remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to provide an integrated molecular, immunological, oxidative, and histopathological evaluation of naturally occurring A. galli infection in Baladi chickens in Cairo, Egypt. A total of 200 Baladi chickens from farmers' households in rural areas of Cairo Governorate were examined between January and June 2026. Gastrointestinal helminths were recovered and identified, and 40 adult nematodes were subjected to molecular confirmation by amplification and bidirectional sequencing of the internal transcribed spacer-1 (ITS-1) region. Phylogenetic analysis was performed to assess the identity of the recovered isolate. Cytokine gene expression and intestinal oxidative stress were evaluated in infected and non-infected birds. Expression of IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, TGF-β, and IFN-γ was quantified by real-time PCR in five birds per group, while intestinal malondialdehyde (MDA), nitric oxide (NO), reduced glutathione (GSH), and catalase (CAT) were assessed as oxidative and antioxidant markers. After serological and molecular screening for concurrent infections, six infected and six non-infected chickens that were free from evidence of other infections were selected for histopathological examination, lesion scoring, intestinal morphometry, and TNF-α immunohistochemistry. A. galli was detected in 90 of 200 chickens, giving an overall prevalence of 45% ((95% CI: 38.1-52.1%). The obtained ITS-1 sequence (GenBank accession PZ363554) clustered within the A. galli clade and showed 99.57-100% nucleotide identity with reference A. galli sequences. Compared with controls, infected birds showed significant upregulation of IL-6 (28.8-fold), IL-8 (30.5-fold), IL-10 (55.9-fold), TGF-β (7.8-fold), and IFN-γ (2.2-fold), with IL-10 showing the greatest increase. Intestinal MDA and NO increased 1.44- and 1.80-fold, respectively, whereas GSH and CAT decreased to 0.76- and 0.28-fold of control levels. Histopathology revealed marked villous degeneration, sloughing and shortening, glandular degeneration, fibrosis, muscular hypertrophy, vascular alterations, and inflammatory cell infiltration. TNF-α immunoreactivity was increased in infected tissues, and morphometric analysis demonstrated alterations in villus dimensions, crypt depth, and the villus-to-crypt ratio. Natural A. galli infection was therefore associated with molecularly confirmed parasitism, altered inflammatory and regulatory cytokine expression, intestinal oxidative imbalance, and pronounced tissue injury in Baladi chickens. This work provides a foundation for experimental studies designed to unravel the causal relationships among these endpoints.

title: Cost-Effectiveness of AI in Breast Cancer Screening and Lung Cancer Diagnostics: A Case Study From Costa Rica.
abstract: Objectives This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness of integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into breast and lung cancer diagnostic workflows in Costa Rica, addressing the scarcity of health economic evidence for AI adoption in low- and middle-income countries and focusing on context-specific systemic barriers. Methods Two state-transition Markov models compared AI-assisted workflows (AI as a first reader) with conventional radiologist-only strategies over a 10-year horizon. AI-supported mammography screening was evaluated in asymptomatic women aged 50 to 70 years. For lung cancer, symptom-driven pathways were modeled using GLOBOCAN 2022 incidence data. Inputs included region-specific costs (USD), quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), and progression probabilities, calibrated to Costa Rica's cancer registry. Methodological rigor adhered to the Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022 guidelines. Results AI in breast cancer screening demonstrated economic dominance: it improved QALYs by 49% (10.46 vs 7.04) and reduced costs by 49% (USD 93 102 vs USD 183 278), yielding a net monetary benefit of USD 212 119 at Costa Rica's willingness-to-pay threshold. For lung cancer, the AI strategy also proved dominant: it reduced total costs to USD 1 218 507 (vs USD 1 337 640) while increasing QALYs to 6.88 (vs 4.15), driven by earlier detection that averts expensive late-stage palliative care. Conclusions AI significantly improved cost-effectiveness in both breast and lung cancer diagnostics, demonstrating economic dominance by mitigating diagnostic delays and reducing late-stage treatment burdens. These findings stress AI's context-dependent impact in low- and middle-income countries and the necessity of early detection investments and equity-focused implementation to align innovation with healthcare system realities.

title: Intestinal ultrasound findings and their prognostic value in patients with eosinophilic gastroenteritis.
abstract: Objective Eosinophilic gastroenteritis (EoGE) is a chronic recurrent disorder with elevated eosinophilic infiltration in the gastrointestinal tract. Objective predictors for disease outcomes are lacking. This study aimed to explore the predictive value of baseline intestinal ultrasound (IUS) along with clinical and laboratory characteristics for disease outcomes. Materials and methods This retrospective cohort study enrolled consecutive patients diagnosed with EoGE at a tertiary medical center between 2019 and 2024. Baseline clinical, laboratory, endoscopy data were collected. IUS images were blindly reviewed for features such as disease location, bowel wall thickness, the "piano key sign" (thickened jejunal folds), and ascites. The primary outcome was steroid-free clinical remission at 12 months. Logistic regression analysis was conducted to reveal the predictive factors. Results This cohort comprised 40 patients with a median age of 34.0 years (IQR, 26.8-52.0 years) and 23 (57.5%) were males. The predominant clinical symptoms included abdominal pain (92.5%), vomiting (52.5%) and diarrhea (47.5%). On IUS, 26 (65.0%) patients showed thickened bowel wall between 4 and 7 mm and predominantly localized in the jejunum (42.5%) and ileum (45.0%). The piano key sign was observed in 12 (30.0%) patients, and ascites was present in 17 (42.5%). Steroid-free clinical remission at 12 months was achieved by 15 (37.5%) patients. On multivariable analysis, the piano key sign (OR 0.092, 95%CI 0.009-0.978, P = 0.048) and vomiting (OR 0.088, 95%CI: 0.017-0.462, P = 0.004) were identified as negative predictors of steroid-free clinical remission with statistical significance, with a combined area under the curve of 0.860. Conclusion The piano key sign on IUS was the negative predictor of steroid-free clinical remission. IUS may provide prognostic information for making personalized treatment and monitoring strategies in EoGE patients.

title: Surgical Anatomy of a Markedly Developed Rhomboid Lip During Cerebellopontine Angle Meningioma Resection: Radiological and Histopathological Correlation.
abstract: Objective The rhomboid lip (RL) is a variable sheet-like neural structure extending from the lateral recess of the fourth ventricle into the cerebellopontine angle (CPA). This technical note describes the radiological, microsurgical, and histopathological features of a markedly developed RL encountered during CPA meningioma surgery, with emphasis on its intraoperative identification and selective surgical management. Methods A 60-year-old woman underwent retrosigmoid resection of a 12-mm left CPA meningioma. Preoperative magnetic resonance imaging suggested a well-developed RL extending from the foramen of Luschka toward the internal auditory canal. Intraoperatively, the RL was assessed according to its morphological features and anatomical relationships and was preserved or selectively divided according to the exposure required during tumor removal. RL tissue that required division for surgical exposure was subsequently examined histopathologically. Results The RL appeared thicker and less transparent than the arachnoid, with veins coursing along its surface. Its relationship with cranial nerve IX and the choroid plexus provided useful anatomical landmarks for identification. The portion overlying the vestibulocochlear nerve was preserved during most of the tumor dissection and divided only when additional exposure was required for complete tumor removal. Histopathological examination demonstrated ependymal and glial layers, confirming the structure as RL. Simpson grade II resection was achieved without new cranial nerve deficits. Conclusions A well-developed RL can be recognized as a distinct anatomical structure using morphological and anatomical landmarks. During CPA surgery, selective preservation or division according to the evolving operative corridor may facilitate anatomically informed surgical dissection.

A well-developed RL can be recognized as a distinct anatomical structure using morphological and anatomical landmarks. During CPA surgery, selective preservation or division according to the evolving operative corridor may facilitate anatomically informed surgical dissection.

title: Imaging And Outcomes In The Treatment Of Sacral Dural Arteriovenous Fistulas.
abstract: Objective Spinal dural arteriovenous fistulas (DAVFs) in the sacral region are extremely rare and their intradural retrograde draining system has not been investigated in detail. The aim of this study was to characterize the venous drainage patterns of sacral DAVFs based on our clinical experience in treating patients with this condition. Methods We retrospectively reviewed the clinical data of patients with sacral DAVFs treated at our institution from January 2016 to January 2024. Preoperative spinal angiography was used to evaluate the positional relationship between the shunt point of sacral DAVF and the vertebral midline. We proposed that if the location of the shunt point was located on the midline, the draining vein would be the filum terminale vein (FTV); if the shunt point was located off the midline, the draining vein would be the radiculomedullary vein (RMV). Results A total of 17 sacral DAVFs patients treated with direct surgery were included in this study. All patients presented with lower extremity weakness and numbness. Sphincter dysfunction was present in 15 patients (88.2%). The mean interval from symptom onset to diagnosis was 14.1 months (range 1-96 months). Preoperative magnetic resonance imaging(MRI) detected T2 hyperintensity at the level of the conus medullaris and intradural flow voids in all patients. Spinal angiography confirmed the diagnosis of sacral DAVF in all cases, and complete fistula occlusion was achieved with surgical ligation in all patients. Intraoperatively, 4 patients with the midline location of the shunt point were confirmed to have FTV as the draining vein, while the other 13 patients with off-midline shunt point were confirmed to have RMV as the draining vein. The intraoperative findings were completely consistent with the preoperative assessment of the draining veins based on the location of the shunt point. Conclusions The draining veins of sacral DAVFs are not always the FTVs, in fact, most sacral DAVFs drain via the RMV. With our simple imaging-based method, the two different types of draining veins in sacral DAVFs can be preliminarily identified before surgery.

title: Classification of Vertebral Artery Course Variations in the Atlantoaxial Region and Their Anatomic Considerations for Surgical Planning: A CTA Imaging Analysis of 511 Patients.
abstract: Background Vertebral artery (VA) course variations in the atlantoaxial region pose significant risks during posterior C1-C2 fixation. This study aimed to classify these variations on CT angiography (CTA) and assess their anatomic implications for surgical planning. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 511 patients (1,022 vertebral arteries) who underwent cervical CTA at Beijing Tongren Hospital between January 2019 and December 2024. Vertebral artery course variations were classified by two independent senior radiologists. Interobserver agreement was assessed using Cohen's kappa coefficient. Associations between variation types and gender/side were analyzed using chi-square tests with adjusted standardized residuals. potential surgical implications were assessed based on anatomical relationships and literature review Results: Seven types were identified: normal type (712 arteries, 70%), high-riding type (243, 24%), posterior arch bridge type (26, 2.5%), protruding type (14, 1.4%), segmental artery type (13, 1.2%), fenestration type (9, 0.9%), and combined type (5, 0.5%). Interobserver agreement was substantial (κ = 0.795). Each type carries distinct anatomic considerations for screw placement, exposure, and surgical approach selection. Conclusions Different vertebral artery course variation types carry distinct and predictable potential surgical implications. Detailed preoperative CTA assessment with three-dimensional reconstruction is essential for identifying these variations and minimizing the risk of iatrogenic vertebral artery injury during posterior atlantoaxial surgery.

title: MRI-Only Preoperative Localization and Semiautomated Three-Dimensional Modeling of the Cervical Vagus Nerve for Vagus Nerve Stimulation Implantation.
abstract: Background We evaluated whether three-dimensional steady-state free precession with time-spatial labeling inversion pulse (3D-SSFP with time-SLIP) MRI could localize the cervical vagus nerve before vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) implantation and developed training-data-free semiautomated vagus nerve tracking software. Methods Thirty patients with drug-resistant epilepsy underwent preoperative cervical 3D-SSFP with time-SLIP MRI followed by VNS implantation. The left vagus nerve was visually identified at the planned surgical level, and its relationship to the common carotid artery (CCA) and internal jugular vein (IJV) was classified. MRI localization was validated against intraoperative findings. A MATLAB-based tool semi-automatically tracked the vagus nerve, CCA, and IJV from user-defined reference points. Accuracy was assessed using coordinate error and classification agreement. Results The vagus nerve was identified on MRI in all 30 patients, with complete concordance between MRI and intraoperative localization. Among 29 classifiable patients, the nerve was located superficially between the CCA and IJV in 45%, superficially and lateral to the CCA in 41%, deep between the CCA and IJV in 10%, and deep and medial to the CCA in 3.4%. The median distance between software-derived and visually identified coordinates was 1 mm (interquartile range, 1-2 mm), and software-derived classification agreed with consensus visual classification in 27 of 29 patients (93%). Conclusions Cervical MRI enabled preoperative localization of the vagus nerve and adjacent vessels. The semiautomated method showed close agreement with expert visual assessment and may support anatomical orientation and surgical planning for VNS implantation.

title: MRI-compatible skull-base pin fixation for advanced image-guided pediatric neurosurgery using augmented reality in infants younger than one year: A feasibility study.
abstract: Background Rigid cranial fixation in infants younger than 1 year is controversial because thin, incompletely ossified calvaria predispose to skull fractures, epidural hematomas, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leaks, and scalp injury. However, neuronavigation, augmented reality (AR), and intraoperative MRI (iMRI) require stable head immobilization. Methods Four infants aged 5, 4, 7, and 10 months underwent surgery for choroid plexus papilloma, pineal atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumor, hemimegalencephaly, and occipital focal cortical dysplasia, respectively. An MRI-compatible head holder served as both fixation device and iMRI coil (prone position n = 3, supine n = 1). Low-pressure skull-base pinning (below 45 N; both lateral sphenoid wings and upper mastoid) avoided thin calvarial regions. Neuronavigation, microscope-based AR, and iMRI were integrated in all cases. Results Stable immobilization sufficient for neuronavigation (registration accuracy below 2 mm), AR-guided microsurgery, and repeated iMRI was achieved in all patients without loss of fixation. iMRI confirmed gross total resection in three cases and complete disconnection on diffusion tensor imaging after hemispherotomy. No fixation-related complications, new or unexpected neurological deficits, or wound-healing disorders occurred during a follow-up of 5-12 months (median 5.5 months). Conclusion In this small technical series, low-pressure skull-base pin fixation with an MRI-compatible head holder provided stable immobilization without fixation-related complications in infants undergoing advanced image-guided neurosurgery. These results demonstrate technical feasibility but do not establish safety, which requires larger studies. Careful skull-base pin placement may reduce classical pinning complications while enabling multimodal neurosurgical techniques in infants.

title: A Stepwise Navigation-Assisted Workflow for Lumbar Biportal Endoscopic Decompression Under Constrained Anatomical Conditions.
abstract: Background Preserving the ligamentum flavum (LF) provides a protective interface but does not create working space. In severe bony stenosis or degenerative spondylolisthesis, the space dorsal to the LF and dura may be insufficient during contralateral lateral-recess decompression, bringing instruments close to the dura. Methods We describe this stepwise workflow for biportal endoscopic decompression under constrained lumbar anatomy. Contralateral cancellous-first drilling creates an intralaminar working recess while the ventral cortex and LF remain intact. The ventral cortex is progressively thinned with the LF preserved as a protective interface. If safely separable, the LF and residual thin cortex are removed; with severe LF-dural adhesion, only a very thin, mobile cortex-ligamentum flavum layer (cortex-LF layer) may remain after the intended bony decompression. Endoscopy guides tissue assessment and LF management; navigation provides adjunctive spatial information. Results The workflow was applied to 13 consecutive cases by a single surgeon. Mean scores, retrospectively collected on a 0-100 mm visual analog scale, decreased from 75 ± 12 to 30 ± 12 for back pain and from 82 ± 9 to 25 ± 11 for leg pain at 3 months. Mean paired reductions were 45 mm (range, 15-70 mm) and 57 mm (range, 30-75 mm), respectively. No intraoperative dural tears or major complications occurred. Conclusions This workflow organizes established protective-layer principles into a conditional sequence for limited dorsal working space. Navigation is adjunctive to endoscopic judgment. This series describes technical feasibility and early clinical experience but does not establish improved safety, reproducibility, or efficacy.

title: Who Benefits From Aggressive Surgery? Predictors of Survival and Short-Term Functional Status After Decompressive Craniectomy for Penetrating Traumatic Brain Injury in the Gaza War: A Consecutive Wartime Cohort.
abstract: Objective Operative series of penetrating traumatic brain injury (pTBI) are vulnerable to treatment-selection bias because patients with adverse features are often managed non-operatively. We evaluated all-cause in-hospital mortality and short-term discharge function in a consecutive wartime cohort under a permissive decompressive craniectomy policy. Methods We retrospectively analyzed a two-center 2025 registry including 151 consecutive patients with CT-confirmed pTBI who underwent decompressive craniectomy. The primary outcome was all-cause in-hospital mortality; the secondary outcome was discharge Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) among survivors with internally consistent entries. Mortality associations were assessed using Fisher exact tests and a 4-covariate Firth penalized logistic model with bootstrap optimism correction and post-hoc intercept recalibration. Results Mortality was 67/147 (46%; 95% CI 37.4-54.0); assigning the 4 unresolved cases as survivors or deaths yielded a whole-cohort range of 44%-47%. Bilaterally fixed and dilated pupils were associated with 10/12 deaths (83%) and remained the only independent predictor in the prespecified model (OR 9.38, 95% CI 1.48-59.4). Transventricular injury carried 13/20 mortality (65%), whereas bihemispheric trajectory was not associated with death. Among 80 survivors, 60 had internally consistent discharge GOS and 41/60 (68%) had GOS 4-5. Three-month GOS was available in only 12/151 patients. Conclusions Severe trajectory features were not uniformly fatal, whereas bilaterally fixed and dilated pupils remained the strongest independent prognostic marker. The findings argue against absolute futility judgments based on trajectory alone. Because discharge function was incompletely ascertained and longer-term follow-up was limited, these data demonstrate survivability under a permissive wartime operative policy rather than long-term functional benefit.

title: SpikeFlow-4D maps rice panicle grain-filling kinetics by computed tomography.
abstract: Rice yield and grain quality depend on the rate, timing, and uniformity of grain filling, yet the spatial dynamics of this process remain difficult to quantify within intact panicles. Destructive sampling reconstructs developmental trajectories from different plants and cannot directly follow how superior and inferior grains fill within the same organ. Here, we developed SpikeFlow-4D, an in situ 4D CT phenotyping framework for non-destructive, repeated monitoring of rice grain filling. The framework integrates coarse-to-fine segmentation, including slice-wise stem detection and removal, morphological cleaning, DBSCAN-based panicle separation, and grain instance extraction, while retaining original 32-bit reconstructed intensities for gray-value quantification and using 8-bit masks only for intermediate segmentation. Applied to two rice cultivars, 9311 and Zhonghua 11 (ZH11), SpikeFlow-4D quantified temporal changes in mean CT gray value, used as a relative attenuation proxy, across the upper, middle, and lower vertical strata of rice panicles. Logistic modeling of the stratum-level trajectories revealed delayed attenuation increase, a shorter active accumulation period than the upper stratum, and a smaller net attenuation increment in the lower stratum of 9311, whereas the estimated peak increase rate did not differ consistently among strata. At 16 days after flowering, the stratum-level CT gray-value pattern was consistent with independently measured grain fresh weight and was positively associated with dry weight across genotype × stratum group means, without establishing a direct calibration between CT gray value and dry-matter content. These results support SpikeFlow-4D as a non-destructive framework for quantifying spatially resolved, population-level grain-filling dynamics in rice panicles.

title: Image-guided focused ultrasound for non-invasive modulation of superficial and deep tissues.
abstract: Focused ultrasound (FUS) enables non-invasive, spatially precise modulation of biological tissues. This protocol describes assembly, calibration, and implementation of a diagnostic ultrasound-guided FUS (dUS-FUS) platform for real-time targeting of superficial and deep tissues in small-animal models. We demonstrate reversible sciatic nerve modulation in a rat acute pain model and assess sensory and motor functions using behavioral tests. The platform provides a reproducible workflow for image-guided tissue modulation and can be adapted to diverse preclinical applications. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Sangwan et al. 1 , 2 .

title: ADHD symptom positivity and its association with medication adherence and psychiatric burden in adults with epilepsy.
abstract: Background Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms are increasingly recognized in adults with epilepsy (AwE) and may contribute to psychiatric burden, seizure-related outcomes, and treatment adherence. We therefore investigated the frequency of ADHD symptom positivity and its associations with medication adherence, psychiatric symptoms, seizure burden, and neurophysiological findings. Methods This cross-sectional study included 100 AwE and 94 healthy controls. ADHD symptoms were assessed using the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS-v1.1). Anxiety and depressive symptoms were evaluated using the Beck Anxiety Inventory and Beck Depression Inventory, respectively. Medication adherence was assessed using the Morisky Medication Adherence Scale (MMAS-8). Participants were classifiedas ASRS-positive or ASRS-negative according to the six-item ASRS Part A screener. Clinical, psychiatric, electroencephalographic, and magnetic resonance imaging findings were compared between groups. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with ADHD-symptom-positivity. Results ADHD-symptom-positivity was significantly more frequent in AwE than in healthy controls (50.0% vs. 25.5%, p = 0.001). Within the epilepsy cohort, ASRS-positive participants demonstrated lower medication adherence (p = 0.010), higher rates of poor adherence (70.0% vs. 48.0%, p = 0.042), higher anxiety (p = 0.002), and depression scores (p < 0.001). Clinically significant anxiety and depression were also more common among ASRS-positive participants (p = 0.027 and p < 0.001, respectively). In multivariable analysis, depression score was independently associated with ADHD-symptom-positivity (OR = 1.147, 95% CI 1.039-1.267, p = 0.007). Conclusions ADHD-symptom-positivity is common in AwE and is associated with poorer medication adherence in the between-group analysis, but this association did not remain statistically significant after multivariable adjustment, while greater psychiatric symptom burden was observed. Routine screening for ADHD-related symptoms may facilitate identification of adults with epilepsy at increased riskfor adverse clinical outcomes and support more comprehensive epilepsy care.
