title: Ultrasound in fetal growth restriction.
abstract: Abstract Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is associated with increased perinatal morbidity and mortality. Its recognition requires differentiation from a constitutionally small-for-gestational-age (SGA) fetus. Based on the current AWMF S2k guideline, this CME review summarizes the ultrasound assessment and clinical management of suspected FGR. Accurate first-trimester dating, standardized fetal biometry, assessment of amniotic fluid volume, and detailed anatomical evaluation form the basis of diagnosis. Consensus-based criteria distinguish early FGR before 32 + 0 weeks' gestation from late FGR at or beyond 32 + 0 weeks' gestation. Multivessel Doppler assessment of the umbilical artery, middle cerebral artery, cerebroplacental ratio, and ductus venosus provides complementary information on placental resistance, fetal redistribution, and cardiovascular decompensation. Cardiotocography, including computerized analysis of short-term variation in early FGR, is used as part of multimodal surveillance and should not be interpreted in isolation. The review discusses appropriate monitoring intervals, indications for inpatient care, antenatal corticosteroids and fetal neuroprotection when preterm birth is anticipated, as well as gestational-age- and finding-dependent timing and mode of delivery. A practical clinical case illustrates the diagnostic pathway from abnormal fetal biometry to delivery planning.

title: Practice Variability in Anorectal Malformations Management across Europe: A TEPS-EUPSA Survey with Analysis of Center Volume Effects.
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate management strategies for anorectal malformations (ARMs) across Europe and assess the impact of institutional case volume on clinical decision-making.A cross-sectional online survey developed within the Trainees in European Pediatric Surgery (TEPS) and endorsed by the European Paediatric Surgeons' Association (EUPSA) Network Office was distributed among pediatric surgeons involved in ARM care. The questionnaire addressed diagnostic workup, surgical management, perioperative care, and long-term follow-up. European responses were analyzed and compared by institutional case volume.A total of 94 responses from 21 countries were analyzed. Substantial variability was observed across all domains of care. Ultrasound-based screening and invertogram were widely used, whereas high-pressure distal colostography was variably applied. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and vaginoscopy were used more selectively. Primary neonatal repair in cases with the rectum located <1 cm from the perineal skin was commonly performed, and staged reconstruction was most frequently undertaken at 3 to 6 months. Non-divided stomas were more frequently used in high-volume centers ( p = 0.002), with increasing center volume associated with higher odds of their use (odds ratio [OR] 2.98, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.51-5.87, p = 0.002). Routine anal dilations were reported by 44.7% of respondents and were less common in high-volume centers ( p = 0.005); increasing volume was associated with lower odds of routine dilation (OR 0.38, 95% CI 0.20-0.72, p = 0.003).ARM management across Europe remains highly variable. Institutional case volume is associated with practice differences, particularly in stoma configuration and postoperative dilation strategies.

title: Mesenteric Vein Thrombosis and Its Interventional-Radiological Management.
abstract: Objective and background Mesenteric venous thrombosis (MVT) is a rare but clinically important cause of mesenteric ischemia. It most often affects the superior mesenteric vein and is associated with high morbidity and mortality. Nonspecific symptoms often delay diagnosis. Severe disease courses may occur in the presence of intestinal infarction. Objective and background The aim of this article is to provide a structured overview of the etiopathogenesis, imaging findings, and interventional radiological treatment options for MVT. Materials and methods Narrative, literature-based review taking into consideration current guidelines, radiological imaging protocols, and endovascular techniques. Results The pathogenesis of MVT can be classified according to Virchow's triad, including hypercoagulability, stasis, and endothelial injury. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) is the method of choice for diagnosis. It demonstrates thrombosis as a contrast filling defect within the portomesenteric venous system and allows assessment of bowel viability. Important CT findings include bowel wall thickening, mesenteric edema, ascites, and the halo or target sign. Pneumatosis intestinalis and portomesenteric venous gas suggest transmural ischemia and indicate the need for immediate surgical management. Systemic anticoagulation is the cornerstone of treatment. Mechanical thrombectomy, local thrombolysis, stent angioplasty, and, where appropriate, TIPS placement may be considered in complex or prolonged clinical courses. Conclusion Early interdisciplinary, imaging-guided management is crucial for diagnosis and treatment planning. CT guides further management by detecting thrombosis and assessing bowel viability. Interventional radiological recanalization is not a first-line treatment, but it may represent an important escalation strategy in selected patients. Key points · Mesenteric venous thrombosis is an uncommon but clinically relevant cause of mesenteric ischemia.. · Early interdisciplinary diagnostic work-up is essential to prevent irreversible intestinal ischemic injury.. · Contrast-enhanced CT represents the key imaging modality, enabling both detection of venous thrombosis and assessment of bowel viability.. · In the absence of contraindications, systemic anticoagulation constitutes the cornerstone of treatment.. · Surgical management is indicated in the presence of suspected transmural bowel necrosis or clinical signs of peritonitis.. · Interventional radiological recanalization techniques may be considered as an escalation strategy in selected patients.. title: A Comprehensive Approach to Flexion-Varus Tibial Plateau Fractures: Principles of Systematic Management.
abstract: Abstract Tibial plateau fractures (TPFs) are complex intra-articular injuries frequently accompanied by significant soft tissue injury. Existing medical literature has shown that TPFs resulting from a flexion-varus injury mechanism, affecting the posteromedial column primarily, are associated with worse clinical outcome scores and a higher risk of conversion to total knee arthroplasty. This narrative review aims to explain why this specific subgroup has a poorer prognosis compared with other TPFs subtypes. Four key factors are examined in this review: fracture morphology, biomechanics, soft tissue involvement, and surgical management. The complex fracture morphology of flexion-varus TPFs can be most accurately assessed using three-dimensional computed tomography-based reconstructions. The mechanism of injury helps to better understand fracture morphology and potential soft tissue injury. Soft tissue injuries are frequent in these type of fractures, such as anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) avulsion fracture, lateral meniscus tears, and entrapment. These three elements are important for better understanding TPFs and adequately planning surgical strategy. The severity of the fracture and the involvement of the posterolateral depression complicate surgical treatment. Visualization of the posteromedial compartment is essential but remains challenging. Anatomical reduction and stable fixation of the posteromedial and posterolaterocentral tibial plateau, with consideration of any meniscal injury, should be performed with care. An ACL avulsion fracture should ideally be fixed. Although preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides valuable information about the soft tissue involved, this examination is not yet routinely performed. Given the high incidence of ACL and (lateral) meniscal injury, an MRI is highly recommended.

title: Interstitial Lung Abnormalities: A Multidisciplinary Narrative Review.
abstract: Abstract Interstitial lung abnormalities (ILAs) is an umbrella term used to describe a spectrum of computed tomography (CT)-detected lung abnormalities that may reflect interstitial lung disease (ILD). Initially perceived as a niche topic-and often underreported in clinical practice-ILAs have gained increasing attention in recent years, given growing evidence of their association with several adverse outcomes, including increased all-cause, respiratory, and cancer-related mortality. Over time, efforts have been made to standardize the definition, classification, and management of ILAs. The recent American Thoracic Society clinical statement has reshaped the definition of ILAs proposed by the Fleischner Society in 2020, introducing substantial changes to the populations in whom ILAs may be identified and proposing new boundaries to distinguish ILAs from ILD. Nevertheless, several key aspects remain debated, and growing efforts are being made to balance the opportunity for early ILD diagnosis against the risk of unnecessary burden on patients and healthcare systems. This is particularly relevant given the increasing number of CT examinations performed in the general population, as well as in patients at increased risk of ILD, such as those with connective tissue disease, and considering the substantial number of examinations related to expanding implementation of lung cancer screening. In this narrative review, we focus on the definition, implications, and management of ILAs, integrating pulmonology, radiology, and pathology perspectives on the strengths and limitations of current approaches.

title: [Molecular-Based Diagnostics and Therapy of Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer (mHSPC)].
abstract: Abstract Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) represents a biologically and clinically heterogeneous disease entity. While traditional clinical parameters such as metastatic burden and timing of metastasis remain prognostically relevant, molecular biomarkers are increasingly gaining importance for individualized treatment planning. Genetic alterations in tumor suppressor genes and DNA repair pathways, particularly BRCA, PTEN, and TP53 aberrations, are associated with more aggressive disease courses and poorer prognosis. At the same time, these molecular alterations provide novel therapeutic opportunities, including the use of PARP inhibitors and AKT inhibitors.In addition to genetic alterations, transcriptomic characteristics also play an important role. In particular, androgen receptor (AR) pathway activity influences prognosis and treatment response. Low AR activity and reduced PSMA expression have been associated with reduced sensitivity to hormonal therapies and increased biological heterogeneity. Conversely, high PSMA expression appears to correlate with improved responses to androgen deprivation therapy as well as PSMA-targeted radioligand therapies.Advanced imaging modalities such as PSMA PET imaging further contribute to a refined understanding of metastatic disease biology and increasingly challenge traditional disease classifications. Moreover, biomarkers including PSA nadir or circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) may help identify progression patterns and guide future treatment intensification or de-escalation strategies.Overall, current evidence suggests that integrating genetic, transcriptomic, and imaging biomarkers may substantially improve the biological characterization of mHSPC. In the future, these approaches could enable a more accurate prognostic stratification and support the development of personalized therapeutic concepts.

Abstract

Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) represents a biologically and clinically heterogeneous disease entity. While traditional clinical parameters such as metastatic burden and timing of metastasis remain prognostically relevant, molecular biomarkers are increasingly gaining importance for individualized treatment planning. Genetic alterations in tumor suppressor genes and DNA repair pathways, particularly BRCA, PTEN, and TP53 aberrations, are associated with more aggressive disease courses and poorer prognosis. At the same time, these molecular alterations provide novel therapeutic opportunities, including the use of PARP inhibitors and AKT inhibitors.In addition to genetic alterations, transcriptomic characteristics also play an important role. In particular, androgen receptor (AR) pathway activity influences prognosis and treatment response. Low AR activity and reduced PSMA expression have been associated with reduced sensitivity to hormonal therapies and increased biological heterogeneity. Conversely, high PSMA expression appears to correlate with improved responses to androgen deprivation therapy as well as PSMA-targeted radioligand therapies.Advanced imaging modalities such as PSMA PET imaging further contribute to a refined understanding of metastatic disease biology and increasingly challenge traditional disease classifications. Moreover, biomarkers including PSA nadir or circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) may help identify progression patterns and guide future treatment intensification or de-escalation strategies.Overall, current evidence suggests that integrating genetic, transcriptomic, and imaging biomarkers may substantially improve the biological characterization of mHSPC. In the future, these approaches could enable a more accurate prognostic stratification and support the development of personalized therapeutic concepts.

title: Ultra-Low-Dose Computed Tomography of the Lung: Evidence and Prospects of a New Method.
abstract: Abstract The introduction of state-of-the-art tube, detector, and image reconstruction techniques has made ultra-low-dose CT (ULD-CT) of the lungs technologically feasible, resulting in radiation exposure comparable to that of chest X-rays. Due to its high-contrast structures, the lung as target organ is generally well suited for reducing radiation exposure while maintaining diagnostic accuracy, which could already be shown for the earlier development of low-dose CT (LDCT). The current state of the literature already demonstrates significant benefits of ULD-CT for the diagnosis of respiratory diseases, including COPD, pneumonia, interstitial lung disease, pediatric lung disease, as well as in interventional procedures. It is expected that ULD-CT will significantly expand the range of indications for CT and, in certain areas, will be able to replace chest X-rays as the initial imaging modality once its availability in institutions increases. Limitations currently arise from the known dependencies of quantitative methods on radiation exposure and image noise, and the fact that in-depth validation has not yet taken place. Key points · Ultra-low-dose computed tomography (ULD-CT) reduces radiation exposure to the level of a conventional chest X-ray through the latest tube, detector, and reconstruction technologies.. · ULD-CT can already be used for the diagnosis of solid pulmonary nodules, pneumonia, and chronic inflammatory airway diseases.. · Especially in children and immunosuppressed patients, ULD-CT should be considered for monitoring the progression of inflammatory lung diseases.. · There is insufficient evidence for the use of ULD-CT in interstitial lung diseases.. · In the future, ULD-CT could replace conventional chest X-ray for many indications in thoracic imaging.. Citation format · Wielpütz MO, Stiller W, Bayerl N et al. Ultra-Low-Dose Computed Tomography of the Lung: Evidence and Prospects of a New Method. Rofo 2026; DOI 10.1055/a-2977-0644.

title: Temporal Bone Osteosarcoma in Pregnancy: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: Introduction Osteosarcoma is the most common primary malignant bone tumor; however, involvement of the temporal bone is exceptionally rare, particularly during pregnancy. The coexistence of malignancy and pregnancy presents unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges requiring multidisciplinary management. Case Presentation A 23-year-old woman presented with persistent right otalgia and an external auditory canal lesion initially diagnosed as cholesteatoma. Following surgical resection, final histopathology revealed temporal bone osteosarcoma with early locoregional recurrence and intracranial extension. Pregnancy was incidentally diagnosed during oncologic evaluation at 24 weeks of gestation. Given the aggressive nature of the tumor, pregnancy termination followed by palliative chemotherapy was initially recommended; however, the patient elected to continue the pregnancy after multidisciplinary counseling. She received chemoradiotherapy with ifosfamide/mesna and 40 Gy radiotherapy. Subsequently, severe anhydramnios and early fetal growth restriction developed, likely secondary to fetal nephrotoxicity associated with ifosfamide exposure. A cesarean section was performed after antenatal corticosteroid administration, resulting in the delivery of a live preterm neonate admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit, and discharged after 58 days of hospitalization. Conclusion Temporal bone osteosarcoma during pregnancy is exceedingly rare and requires complex multidisciplinary management balancing maternal oncologic treatment and fetal risks.

title: Giant Multiloculated Cystic Trochlear Nerve Schwannoma Between the Tentorial Leaflets: Case Report and Systematic Review.
abstract: Background Trochlear nerve schwannomas (TNSs) are exceptionally rare benign tumors, accounting for a very small fraction of intracranial schwannomas. Due to their deep locations and slow growth, they often reach a considerable size before diagnosis. Giant or multiloculated cystic variants are exceptionally uncommon and present significant diagnostic and surgical challenges. Methods A 32-year-old female presented with headache and dizziness but no diplopia. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed a giant multiloculated cystic lesion extending from the posterior fossa to the right temporal lobe, causing obstructive hydrocephalus. The mass was removed through a right paramedian supracerebellar transtentorial approach under intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring. The tumor was confined between the two tentorium leaflets, with the trochlear nerve entering and exiting the lesion. Gross total resection was achieved with an uneventful postoperative course. Histopathology confirmed a World Health Organization Grade I schwannoma with Antoni A-B architecture and diffuse S-100 positivity. A systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (2020) guidelines, identifying 45 surgically treated cases, analyzed together with the present case ( n = 46). Results The mean age was 44.7 years, with an approximately equal sex distribution. Most tumors (76.1%) were located in the ambient or crural cisterns, followed by the quadrigeminal cistern (10.8%) and cisterno-cavernous region (8.7%). Diplopia and trochlear nerve palsy were the most common presenting symptoms. Gross total resection was achieved in 80.4% of patients, while postoperative trochlear palsy occurred in 60.8%. No malignant transformation or early recurrence was reported. Conclusion This case represents one of the largest TNSs described and the second known lesion arising between the tentorial leaflets. Awareness of this unique anatomic configuration is essential for accurate preoperative diagnosis and surgical planning. A meticulous, anatomy-guided microsurgical approach enables complete resection while preserving neurological function in select cases.

title: Neurological prognostication after cardiac arrest: evidence review and institutional protocol proposal.
abstract: Background Cardiac arrest (CA) is associated with high mortality and neurological morbidity, mainly due to hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. Accurate neurological prognostication in CA survivors is essential to guide therapeutic decisions and provide appropriate care. Objective To review the current evidence on neurological prognostication after CA and to propose an institutional protocol adapted to the resources of Hospital de Clínicas de Porto Alegre (HCPA). Methods The current narrative review was conducted in two stages: a literature review and the development of an institutional protocol. Articles were selected according to their clinical relevance and their contribution to current evidence on neurological prognostication after CA. The PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and SciELO databases were searched. The protocol was developed considering the clinical tools available at HCPA, including neurological examination, electroencephalography (EEG), and neuroimaging. Results Brain injury after CA occurs in three stages: intra-arrest ischemia, immediate reperfusion, and delayed postreperfusion injury. Prognostic modalities include neurological examination, EEG, somatosensory-evoked potentials (SSEPs), serum biomarkers, and neuroimaging. Reliable predictors of poor outcome include absent brainstem reflexes at 72 hours, persistent EEG suppression, bilateral absence of cortical N20 potentials, and diffuse abnormalities on magnetic resonance imaging. The proposed protocol organizes assessments from admission to the Intensive Care Unit through day 5 after the return of spontaneous circulation. Conclusion A standardized post-CA neurological prognostication protocol at HCPA may improve care quality, enhance communication with families, and support ethically-sound decision-making.

title: Automated Detection and Segmentation of Dental Caries in Panoramic Radiographs Using YOLOv8-Based Deep Learning Model.
abstract: Objectives This study aimed to develop an automated dental caries localization system through detection and classification using a deep learning (DL) approach based on You Only Look Once Version 8 (YOLOv8). Materials and methods YOLOv8 models were developed using 750 panoramic radiographs, which were divided into training, validation, and test sets at a ratio of 80%:10%:10%. The training and validation data were cropped into six regions to enhance the detection model performance. Confusion matrices were utilized to assess performance metrics, including accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1 score. Statistical analysis Fleiss's kappa was used to evaluate overall agreement among the YOLOv8 predictions and the expert evaluations, followed by Cohen's kappa for each comparison category. Results For caries detection, the YOLOv8-M model achieved an optimal accuracy of 95.22%, a sensitivity of 84.07%, a specificity of 98.18%, a precision of 92.46%, and an F1 score of 88.06%. For segmentation, the YOLOv8-X model achieved an optimal accuracy of 93.92%, a sensitivity of 78.30%, a specificity of 98.01%, a precision of 91.15%, and an F1 score of 84.24%. Fleiss's kappa analysis indicated substantial agreement of 0.766 ( p < 0.001) between model predictions and expert evaluations. Conclusion The YOLOv8 models demonstrated strong performance in detecting and segmenting dental caries in panoramic radiographs. They also showed substantial agreement with expert assessments, highlighting their potential as a reliable tool for automated caries identification. Further development is recommended to enhance performance, particularly by reducing false positive and false negative cases.

title: Legal and Regulatory Considerations for Artificial Intelligence Use in Medical and Radiology Research.
abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into medical imaging and radiology research, improving image acquisition, interpretation, workflow efficiency, and decision support. However, its rapid adoption has introduced complex legal and regulatory challenges involving patient privacy, data governance, algorithm validation, liability, intellectual property, transparency, cybersecurity, and ethical oversight. A comprehensive understanding of the evolving legal landscape is essential for the safe, effective, and legally compliant implementation of AI in radiology. Methods A narrative review of the published literature and current regulatory guidance was conducted. Relevant international legal and regulatory frameworks governing AI in medical imaging were evaluated, including the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, General Data Protection Regulation, U.S. Food and Drug Administration guidance on Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, World Health Organization recommendations, International Medical Device Regulators Forum principles, and selected national regulations. Key topics reviewed included data protection, informed consent, AI validation, regulatory approval pathways, post-market surveillance, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, explainability, and medico-legal responsibility. Results Current regulatory frameworks increasingly classify AI-enabled radiology software as SaMD, requiring risk-based evaluation, clinical validation, quality management systems, and continuous post-market performance monitoring. Regulatory authorities emphasize transparency, human oversight, data security, and lifecycle governance of AI systems. Nevertheless, important legal challenges remain, including liability for AI-assisted diagnostic errors, ownership of AI-generated outputs, secondary use of imaging data, cross-border data sharing, algorithmic bias, and regulation of adaptive or continuously learning AI models. Conclusions The legal framework governing AI in radiology is evolving in parallel with technological innovation. Responsible integration of AI into clinical practice and research requires harmonized international regulations, robust data governance, standardized validation protocols, transparent algorithm development, and clearly defined legal accountability. Continued collaboration among radiologists, researchers, regulators, policymakers, industry, and legal experts will be essential to ensure that AI technologies remain safe, ethical, equitable, and trustworthy while maximizing their potential to improve patient care.

originalAbstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into medical imaging and radiology research, improving image acquisition, interpretation, workflow efficiency, and decision support. However, its rapid adoption has introduced complex legal and regulatory challenges involving patient privacy, data governance, algorithm validation, liability, intellectual property, transparency, cybersecurity, and ethical oversight. A comprehensive understanding of the evolving legal landscape is essential for the safe, effective, and legally compliant implementation of AI in radiology.

Methods

A narrative review of the published literature and current regulatory guidance was conducted. Relevant international legal and regulatory frameworks governing AI in medical imaging were evaluated, including the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, General Data Protection Regulation, U.S. Food and Drug Administration guidance on Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, World Health Organization recommendations, International Medical Device Regulators Forum principles, and selected national regulations. Key topics reviewed included data protection, informed consent, AI validation, regulatory approval pathways, post-market surveillance, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, explainability, and medico-legal responsibility.

Results

Current regulatory frameworks increasingly classify AI-enabled radiology software as SaMD, requiring risk-based evaluation, clinical validation, quality management systems, and continuous post-market performance monitoring. Regulatory authorities emphasize transparency, human oversight, data security, and lifecycle governance of AI systems. Nevertheless, important legal challenges remain, including liability for AI-assisted diagnostic errors, ownership of AI-generated outputs, secondary use of imaging data, cross-border data sharing, algorithmic bias, and regulation of adaptive or continuously learning AI models.

Conclusions

The legal framework governing AI in radiology is evolving in parallel with technological innovation. Responsible integration of AI into clinical practice and research requires harmonized international regulations, robust data governance, standardized validation protocols, transparent algorithm development, and clearly defined legal accountability. Continued collaboration among radiologists, researchers, regulators, policymakers, industry, and legal experts will be essential to ensure that AI technologies remain safe, ethical, equitable, and trustworthy while maximizing their potential to improve patient care.

title: The role of thoracic interventional radiologists in the management of chest infections: a pictorial review.
abstract: Thoracic infections remain a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, requiring accurate and timely diagnosis to guide appropriate treatment. This pictorial review illustrates the role of the interventional thoracic radiologist in the management of infectious processes involving the lung, pleura, mediastinum, and chest wall. We describe a range of non-vascular image-guided percutaneous diagnostic and therapeutic techniques. These include targeted sampling for microbiological identification in complicated pneumonias and cavitary lesions, as well as image-guided drainage of pulmonary, pleural, mediastinal, and thoracic wall infectious collections. The advantages of these minimally invasive percutaneous techniques, especially in peripheral/subpleural lung lesions, are highlighted. In addition, we present practical technical considerations and diagnostic "tips and tricks," aimed at improving diagnostic yield. By integrating imaging findings with interventional strategies, this review underscores the growing clinical impact of interventional radiology in thoracic infections.

title: Vestibular manifestations as the initial presentation of multiple sclerosis: a case series.
abstract: Background Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic demyelinating disease of the central nervous system that can initially present with diverse neurological symptoms. Vestibular dysfunction may be an early manifestation, and can mimic common peripheral vestibular disorders, creating a diagnostic challenge. Objectives To characterize vestibular symptoms and clinical signs in patients with MS presenting initially with vestibular dysfunction. Materials and methods This retrospective observational case series included ten patients evaluated between 2019 and 2024 whose first clinical manifestation of MS was vestibular dysfunction. Clinical and neuro-otologic assessment, vHIT, and VNG were performed, and brain MRI was obtained when central vestibular involvement was suspected. Results Four main presentations were identified: acute vestibular syndrome ( n = 2), imbalance ( n = 4), recurrent vertigo ( n = 2), and positional vertigo ( n = 2). Nine of ten patients had at least one finding suggestive of central vestibular involvement, whereas one patient had a normal vestibular examination. Brain MRI demonstrated lesions fulfilling the radiological criteria for MS in all ten patients. Conclusions Central vestibular signs in young adults presenting with vestibular symptoms should raise suspicion of an underlying central lesion and possible MS. Recognition of these signs, together with appropriate neuroimaging when clinically indicated, may facilitate earlier diagnosis during the clinically isolated syndrome stage.

title: Multimodal based Brain Tumor Classification using Clustered Federated Learning in Edge based IoT Network.
abstract: A brain tumor is characterized by the uncontrolled growth of cells that causes a severe impact on the quality of life. Nowadays, various methods based on multimodal medical images are used to identify brain tumors. Meanwhile, these methods require extensive amounts of labeled information to identify disease tissues and often encounter various challenges based on privacy and accuracy. This paper establishes a Taylor-based Focal Log-cosh Entropy Network (TFLE-Net) to classify brain tumors from demographic data and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) images by utilizing clustered federated learning in an edge-based Internet of Things (IoT) network. The detection process is executed in clustered federated learning concerning two entities: server and nodes. In a local training model, an input MRI scan is pre-processed, further brain tumor areas are segmented, and then, the mining of various features is performed. Simultaneously, the normalization of input demographic data is done, and the suitable features are selected using information gain. Further, the extracted features and chosen features are subjected to TFLE-Net to classify brain tumors. Additionally, the TFLE-Net yielded Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.057, Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.047, True Positive Rate (TPR) of 97.789%, and accuracy of 96.987%.

title: Benchmarking 3D U-Net variants for volumetric segmentation of the substantia nigra and brain ageing related analysis using 7T MRI.
abstract: Objective: Accurate segmentation of the substantia nigra (SN) is essential for assessing its structural integrity and volumetric changes in Parkinson's disease and brain aging. However, it remains challenging due to SN's small size, deep location, and low contrast on conventional MRI. This study benchmarked six U-Net variants baseline 3D U-Net, ResU-Net, SE-U-Net, Attention U-Net, U-Net++, and U-Net 3+ for SN segmentation using ultra-high-field 7 T MRI. Methods T1-weighted MP2RAGE images from the ATAG dataset (53 healthy subjects: 31 train, 7 validation and 15 test). Six architectures were evaluated: 3D U-Net, ResU-Net, SE-U-Net, Attention U-Net, U-Net++, and U-Net 3+.Performance was evalauted with Dice score, IoU, 95% HD95, ASSD, and also age-stratified analysis was considered for analysing the robustness of model across young, middle-aged, and elderly cohorts. Results While ResU-Net achieved the highest overlap metrics (Dice = 0.763, IoU = 0.618), where the baseline 3D U-Net outperformed all variants in boundary accuracy (HD95 = 13.85 mm, ASSD = 20.15 mm). The U-Net 3+ and SE-U-Net complex models relatively underperformed, indicated that architectural complexity does not enhance the segmentation performance of small subcortical structures. Descriptive Age-stratified analysis shows, ResU-Net maintained consistent performance across different age groups and 3D U-Net revealed strong age-invariance, however no statistically significant age-group differences were exhibited. Conclusions This study findings demonstrates architecture selection influences overlap, boundary detection and volume estimation small-structure segmentation and highlights the importance of evaluating model robustness to demographic variability. The findings offer a methodological benchmark for developing reliable SN volumetry tools for neurodegenerative research.

title: Long-segment posterior spinal instrumentation with intracanal bone fragment compaction for indirect anterior column support: a single-arm feasibility study in high load-sharing classification score thoracolumbar burst fractures.
abstract: Background Thoracolumbar burst fractures with high Load Sharing Classification (LSC) scores are mechanically unstable and associated with severe vertebral comminution and failure risk after short-segment fixation. This study evaluated outcomes of long-segment posterior fixation combined with intracanal bone fragment compaction as an indirect means of supporting the anterior column. Methods This retrospective study analyzed prospectively collected data from 121 consecutive patients with unstable thoracolumbar burst fractures (T10-L2) and LSC scores >6. All patients underwent open long-segment posterior instrumentation, decompression, and compaction of retropulsed intracanal bone fragments. Radiological outcomes included Cobb angle, percentage of anterior height compression (PAHC), vertebral body compression ratio (VBCR), and spinal canal compromise. Neurological recovery was assessed using the American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) scale, and functional outcomes using the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). Results The cohort included 70 men and 51 women, with a mean age of 37.2 years and follow-up of 23.2 months. At final follow-up, 58.7% (95% CI 49.8-67.1%) achieved ASIA grade E. Significant improvements were observed in VBCR, PAHC, Cobb angle (15.6° to 7.9°; p = 0.008), and spinal canal compromise (65.2% to 8.7%; p < 0.001). Mean ODI improved from 59.4 to 8.4 ( p < 0.001). Conclusion Long-segment posterior fixation with intracanal bone fragment compaction was associated with favorable short- to mid-term neurological, functional, and radiological outcomes. Prospective comparative studies with CT-based fusion assessment, standardized safety reporting, and longer follow-up are required to confirm effectiveness and durability.

title: Impact of cerebral venous outflow on futile recanalization despite complete reperfusion following mechanical thrombectomy.
abstract: Background A substantial proportion of patients with acute ischemic stroke remain functionally dependent despite complete angiographic reperfusion (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] 3) after mechanical thrombectomy (MT). This mismatch, commonly termed futile recanalization, may reflect tissue-level hypoperfusion not captured by arterial reperfusion grading. We investigated whether cerebral venous outflow, assessed using the Cortical Vein Opacification Score (COVES), provides prognostic information beyond conventional clinical and arterial imaging variables. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 420 adults with anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion who underwent MT between 2015-2025 and achieved mTICI 3 reperfusion. Venous outflow was graded on baseline computed tomography angiography using COVES. Futile recanalization was defined as a 90-day modified Rankin Scale score of 3-6. Independent associations with futile recanalization were evaluated using multivariable binary logistic regression. Results Futile recanalization occurred in 191 patients (45.5%). After adjustment for age, admission NIHSS, ASPECTS, total passes, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, previous stroke, and arterial collateral status, higher COVES remained independently associated with lower odds of futile recanalization (OR per 1-point increase, 0.649; 95% CI, 0.537-0.784; p < 0.001). Age (OR, 1.031; p = 0.005), admission NIHSS (OR, 1.091; p = 0.001), and total passes (OR, 1.538; p < 0.001) were independently associated with higher odds of futile recanalization. Arterial collateral status was not independently associated with outcome. COVES showed greater discrimination than admission NIHSS (AUC, 0.742 vs 0.624). Conclusions Baseline COVES was independently associated with 90-day functional outcome among patients achieving complete reperfusion after MT. COVES may serve as a complementary prognostic imaging marker rather than a treatment-selection tool. Prospective external validation is required.

title: GATA3-positive primary ductal adenocarcinoma of the lacrimal gland with calcification: a case report.
abstract: Primary ductal adenocarcinoma of the lacrimal gland (PDALG) is a rare epithelial malignancy of the ocular adnexa. A man in his 50s presented with painless swelling of the right upper eyelid and was found to have a right lacrimal gland mass with punctate hyperdense foci on computed tomography (CT) and low signal intensity on both T1- and T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging. Histopathology of the tumor revealed nest-like, cribriform, and tubular proliferation of atypical epithelial cells, with fibrotic and hyalinized stroma, comedo necrosis, and calcification. Immunohistochemistry showed positivity for androgen receptor, HER2, and GATA3, while GCDFP-15 was negative. Positron emission tomography-computed tomography showed no systemic lesions, supporting the diagnosis of PDALG. Elastica van Gieson staining demonstrated venous invasion, and adjuvant radiotherapy was performed after complete excision. This case illustrates the diagnostic value of correlating punctate hyperdensity on CT with pathologic calcification and integrating GATA3/HER2 findings with the systemic exclusion of metastatic breast carcinoma. At 1 year of follow-up, no local recurrence or distant metastasis had been detected; however, given the potential for late metastasis in this pathology, long-term close observation is required.

title: Deep learning-based segmentation of non-perfused volume after magnetic resonance guided high-intensity focused ultrasound therapies: a retrospective evaluation on clinical patient data.
abstract: Introduction Non-perfused volume (NPV) is a key imaging biomarker for treatment efficacy in MR -guided high-intensity focused ultrasound (MR-HIFU). In uterine fibroids therapies, the NPV ratio is strongly associated with clinical outcomes and long-term efficacy. We developed and clinically evaluated a deep learning-based automatic NPV segmentation model to facilitate standardized and efficient post-treatment assessment. Materials and methods Contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MR images from 79 patients treated with MR-HIFU were retrospectively analyzed, with NPVs manually delineated as the reference. A 2D U-Net convolutional neural network was optimized using a Tversky loss function (α = 0.7) to prioritize volumetric robustness. Performance was evaluated using similarity metrics (Dice coefficient [DC], 95th percentile Hausdorff distance [HD95]) and clinically relevant measures, including Bland-Altman analysis of volumetric quantification error, precision, recall, slice-level missing rate, and processing time. Results In the independent test cohort ( n = 12), the model achieved a median DC of 0.900 (IQR: 0.841-0.920) and a median HD95 of 0.42 (IQR: 0.32-0.60) mm. Median absolute NPV quantification error was 4.3 mL (IQR: 2.6-8.4 mL), corresponding to a median relative error of 2.3% (IQR: -2.4% - 10.5%). Precision and recall were 0.909 (IQR: 0.843-0.940) and 0.912 (IQR: 0.881-0.931), respectively, with 2.8% of ground truth-positive slices missed. Average processing time per patient (∼384 slices) was 1-2 min. Conclusion The proposed 2D U-Net provides accurate and time-efficient automatic NPV segmentation. Quantitative and clinically oriented evaluation demonstrates reliable volumetric assessment with minimal slice-level omission, supporting integration into routine MR-HIFU treatment workflows.

title: Successful treatment of an aggressive vertebral haemangioma with radiofrequency ablation and laminectomy: a case report.
abstract: Background and importance Aggressive vertebral haemangiomas are rare, hypervascular spinal tumours that can extend beyond the vertebral body, causing spinal cord compression and neurological deficits. These lesions are particularly challenging to manage due to high intraoperative bleeding risk. Although treatments like embolisation, radiotherapy, and surgical decompression have been employed, each carries limitations. Radiofrequency ablation (RFA), commonly used in metastatic spine disease, offers a targeted approach to devascularise lesions prior to surgery and may reduce perioperative morbidity. Clinical presentation A 17-year-old female presented with a three-week history of ascending lower limb numbness, gait ataxia, and recurrent falls. Examination revealed right lower limb weakness and sensory loss up to T5/6. MRI demonstrated an aggressive haemangioma of the T3 vertebra with extension into posterior elements and dorsal epidural compression. Given progressive symptoms, she underwent transpedicular RFA using a thermocouple-guided probe, followed by cement vertebroplasty and laminectomy (T1-T3). Intraoperatively, the posterior tumour component was unexpectedly absent, supporting the hypothesis that it collapsed following devascularisation. Neurological recovery progressed with structured physiotherapy, and no recurrence was noted on two-year follow-up imaging. title: Contralateral acute subdural hematoma following moyamoya bypass surgery: a rare complication.
abstract: Background Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a progressive cerebrovascular disorder characterized by compensatory development of collateral vessels in response to internal carotid artery occlusion. Superficial temporal artery to middle cerebral artery (STA-MCA) bypass combined with encephalomyosynangiosis is a standard surgical intervention, hemorrhagic complications following such procedures are rare, especially in pediatric patients. We present a rare case of contralateral acute subdural hematoma (ASDH) occurring immediately after revascularization surgery in a child with MMD. Case description A 7-year-old girl with a history of left cerebral infarction due to MMD underwent left STA-MCA bypass with encephalomyosynangiosis. Although the bypass was technically successful and the patient showed no new neurological deficits postoperatively, routine computed tomography revealed a contralateral ASDH. The hematoma was promptly evacuated. Intraoperative findings included oozing from the dura near the sphenoid ridge, but no active bleeding source was identified. She recovered well without neurological deterioration. Notably, follow-up digital subtraction angiography at five months postoperatively revealed the formation of a spontaneous transdural anastomosis from the right middle meningeal artery, eliminating the need for further bypass surgery on the contralateral side. Conclusion Cerebral atrophy, intraoperative cerebrospinal fluid drainage, and perioperative aspirin use may have contributed to the development of contralateral ASDH. Surgeons should be aware of this possibility. Prompt recognition and evacuation are essential.

title: Diagnostic utility of the HAS-GCA score versus other Southend Giant Cell Arteritis Probability Score-ultrasound prediction models in giant cell arteritis.
abstract: Objective The aim of this study was to validate the HAS-GCA score, a prediction model combining the Southend Giant Cell Arteritis Probability Score (SGCAPS) with ultrasonography (US) halo count, and compare its diagnostic utility with other prediction models combining SGCAPS with US scores for diagnosing giant cell arteritis (GCA). Method : Treatment-naïve patients with suspected GCA were prospectively included in an observational cohort and underwent clinical assessment, including temporal artery biopsy (TAB) and pretreatment US and [ 18 F]fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography/computed tomography. The clinical diagnosis was confirmed after 24 weeks. Baseline data were assessed to calculate SGCAPS. Three prediction models combining SGCAPS with US scores - halo score, OMERACT GCA ultrasound score (OGUS), and halo count - were applied to classify patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-probability categories of GCA. The ability of the prediction models to correctly classify patients into low- and high-probability categories, and the proportion of patients with intermediate probability requiring additional tests, were compared. Results : GCA diagnosis was confirmed in 60/99 patients (61%). Prediction models based on halo count (HAS-GCA score), halo score, and OGUS had similar misclassification rates of 3%; HAS-GCA score had the lowest proportion of patients with intermediate probability (39% vs 47% and 59%, respectively). Conclusion : The HAS-GCA prediction model reliably stratified patients with suspected GCA into low- and high-probability categories, enabling confidence in ruling in or ruling out the GCA diagnosis. However, almost half of the patients required further evaluation to establish a correct diagnosis.

title: Differential diagnostic value of PAX1 and JAM3 methylation for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia between premenopausal and postmenopausal women: a retrospective clinical study in China.
abstract: PAX1/JAM3 methylation are promising biomarkers for high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) detection, but menopausal status may affect diagnostic accuracy. This retrospective study compared their clinical performance between premenopausal and postmenopausal women undergoing colposcopy. 705 women undergoing colposcopy for abnormal screening results and/or clinical symptoms were stratified by menopausal status, including 192 postmenopausal and 513 premenopausal women. Subjects were further classified into ≤CIN1 and CIN2+ groups according to histopathology. Diagnostic and triage utility of PAX1/JAM3 methylation for identifying CIN2+ lesions were compared between premenopausal and postmenopausal women. PAX1/JAM3 methylation demonstrated superior diagnostic performance for CIN2+ detection in postmenopausal women compared with premenopausal women, either alone or in combination. Sensitivities of PAX1m and JAM3m in postmenopausal women (90.00%, 95% CI: 76.34-97.21%; 82.50%, 95% CI: 67.22-92.66%) were higher than those in premenopausal women (61.98%, 95% CI: 52.71-70.65%; 60.33%, 95% CI: 51.04-69.11%) (all p < 0.05). The combination improved sensitivity to 72.73% in premenopausal women and maintained 92.50% in postmenopausal women. Besides, PAX1/JAM3 methylation outperformed cytology and HPV16/18 testing in both groups (p < 0.001). In HPV16/18-positive or cytology triage, methylation increased positive predictive values (PPVs) for CIN2+/CIN3+ and reduced colposcopy referrals . However, CIN2+ missed rates in premenopausal women (27.54% for HPV16/18-positive triage and 23.85% for cytology triage) were higher than those in postmenopausal counterparts. The diagnostic performance of PAX1/JAM3 methylation for high-grade cervical lesions differs distinctly between premenopausal and postmenopausal women undergoing colposcopy. Menopausal status should be considered when applying methylation biomarkers, particularly as a valuable auxiliary tool to improve diagnostic accuracy in elderly women.

title: Temporal trends in incidence, clinical characteristics and outcomes of pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis in Southern Denmark from 2009 to 2022: a retrospective population-based cohort study.
abstract: Objectives Pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis (PVO) is a severe infection with increasing incidence. We aimed to describe long-term population-based temporal trends in incidence, clinical presentation, diagnostic approaches, microbiology, and outcomes. Materials and methods We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study including 1,017 adults with multidisciplinary team-verified PVO diagnosed at a tertiary infectious diseases referral centre in the Region of Southern Denmark between 2009 and 2022. Incidence rates (IRs) per 100,000 person-years (PY) were calculated using regional population data and compared across three calendar periods (2009-2013, 2014-2018, 2019-2022). Temporal changes in clinical characteristics, microbiology, diagnostic strategies, and outcomes were assessed. Results In total, 1,017 patients were included. The crude IR increased from 4.7 per 100,000 PY in 2009-2013 to 11.0 in 2019-2022, with the largest increase among patients aged ≥70 years. Mean age and comorbidity burden rose over time. Pain was common, fever was often absent, and neurological deficits occurred in 33.5% ( n = 341). Postsurgical infection was the most frequent primary focus, and concomitant endocarditis occurred in 8.3% ( n = 84). A microbiological diagnosis was established in 64.8% ( n = 635) of cases, most commonly Staphylococcus aureus . Use of Fluorine-18 Fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography ([ 18 F]FDG-PET/CT) increased over time. Median hospital stay remained 33 days. One-year mortality increased from 9.5% to 18.2%, while relapse declined, resulting in a stable composite risk of death or relapse (20.7%). Conclusions The incidence of PVO increased markedly from 2009 to 2022, predominantly in older patients with comorbidities. Despite improved diagnostics, microbiologically-negative cases remain frequent. Mortality remained high and increased over time.

title: Development full-thickness macular hole and exudative retinal detachment in central retinal vein occlusion after intravitreal ranibizumab.
abstract: Background Intravitreal injection of anti‑vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) has become a first-line treatment for macular oedema secondary to central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO). However, there have been recent reports of a surprising complication associated with intravitreal injection of anti-VEGF. We report a case of full-thickness macular hole (FTMH) and exudative retinal detachment (ERD) after intravitreal injection of ranibizumab for macular oedema. Case presentation A 21-year-old patient with macular oedema secondary to CRVO developed FTMH and ERD in her left eye after the first intravitreal injection of ranibizumab. A 25 G vitrectomy was performed, during which the internal limiting membrane was peeled off followed by filling with silicone oil tamponade. One week after the operation, optical coherence tomography showed closure of the macular hole. Conclusion Although vitrectomy combined with removal of the inner limiting membrane can reclose macular hole caused by intravitreal injection of anti-VEGF drugs, these cases of FTMH differ from those of idiopathic FTMH in having a poorer visual prognosis. Ophthalmologists should be vigilant in monitoring the possibility of inducing macular hole through treatment with ranibizumab. In addition, ERD associated with CRVO represents a serious vision-threatening complication that merits close clinical attention from ophthalmologists.

title: Clinical Spectrum and Insights from One Year of Ocular Genetics at a Single Tertiary Eye Care Centre.
abstract: Introduction Genetic testing benefits individuals and families with inherited eye diseases by facilitating accurate diagnosis, informing prognosis, enabling assessment for at-risk family members, and supporting targeted therapies. This study aimed to characterize the spectrum of inherited eye disorders and evaluate the diagnostic yield of genetic testing at a single tertiary eye care centre over a one-year period. Methods A retrospective review of patients attending the ocular genetics service at a tertiary eye care centre in India from January 1 to December 31, 2024, was conducted. Results Of 1325 patients evaluated, 862 (65%) underwent genetic testing. Inherited retinal disorders were the most common ( n = 440, 51%), followed by cornea and anterior segment disorders ( n = 107, 12.4%). Other conditions included hereditary optic nerve disorders ( n = 75, 8.7%), glaucoma ( n = 70, 8.1%), lenticular disorders ( n = 54, 6.3%), phacomatoses ( n = 25, 2.9%), ocular tumours ( n = 20, 2.3%), strabismus and albinism ( n = 19 and 18; ~2% each), MAC spectrum disorders ( n = 10, 1.4%), and systemic syndromes ( n = 22, 2.5%). Diagnostic yield was achieved in 605 (70%), while 257 (30%) remained inconclusive. Of the 463 untested families, the motivations were unascertained reasons ( n = 156, 33%), financial constraints ( n = 138, 30%), intent to test later ( n = 90, 19%), and belief that no treatment was available ( n = 79, 17%). Discussion Inherited retinal and anterior segment disorders constitute the most frequent genetic eye diseases. Genetic testing has enabled genotype-phenotype correlation in over two-thirds of cases. Financial constraints and limited availability of disease-modifying treatments remain key barriers for uptake of genetic testing.

title: Comparison of joint space volume according to the status of temporomandibular joint internal derangement.
abstract: Objective To evaluate cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-based three-dimensional joint space volume according to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-defined temporomandibular joint (TMJ) internal derangement (ID). Methods Ninety-one TMJs from 48 patients were classified as normal, anterior disc displacement with reduction (ADcR), or without reduction (ADsR). CBCT-derived volumes were compared using linear mixed-effects models, with additional adjustment for age, sex, osseous degeneration, and joint pain. Results Unadjusted analyses showed significant group differences in total joint space, condylar, glenoid fossa, anterior, and medial joint-space volumes. After multivariable adjustment, no volumetric outcome showed a significant overall between-group difference. Conclusion CBCT-derived volumetric differences were observed among MRI-defined disc displacement groups but were attenuated after adjustment for demographic and clinical factors. CBCT may provide complementary information on TMJ morphology but cannot directly assess disc position and should not replace MRI.

title: Multi-label classification of temporomandibular joint osteoarthritic changes on CBCT: An anatomically guided artificial intelligence framework.
abstract: Objective To develop and evaluate an anatomically guided artificial intelligence framework for joint-level detection and multi-label characterization of temporomandibular joint (TMJ) osteoarthritic changes on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). Methods CBCT examinations from 71 patients (142 TMJs) were assessed independently by two expert readers for erosion, osteophyte formation, subchondral sclerosis, subchondral cysts, joint-space narrowing, and condylar flattening. Discordant cases underwent third-reader adjudication to establish the reference standard. A 3-dimensional ResNet18 model was trained using patient-level training, validation, and independent test partitions. Joint-level OA-associated features were evaluated. Complete TMJ region-of-interest (ROI) and segmentation-masked condyle inputs were compared. Condylar flattening was analyzed separately. Results Inter-reader agreement varied by feature, ranging from slight agreement for flattening (κ = -0.01) and joint-space narrowing (κ = 0.15) to substantial agreement for osteophyte formation (κ = 0.63). Automated condyle segmentation achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 0.91 ± 0.042. The joint-level model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.9325, with sensitivity of 0.8470 and specificity of 0.9081. Feature-level AUCs ranged from 0.6756 to 0.9515. Segmentation-masked condyle input yielded higher classification of erosion (AUC, 0.8685), osteophyte formation (0.9090), subchondral sclerosis (0.9134), and subchondral cysts (0.9515), whereas complete TMJ ROI input performed better for joint-space narrowing (0.8132). Conclusions This framework extends CBCT assessment beyond binary detection of TMJ OA-associated changes by providing feature-level characterization. Anatomically guided masking showed higher AUCs for abnormalities intrinsic to the mandibular condyle, whereas joint-space narrowing performed better with broader joint context. These observations require confirmation in larger datasets.

CBCT examinations from 71 patients (142 TMJs) were assessed independently by two expert readers for erosion, osteophyte formation, subchondral sclerosis, subchondral cysts, joint-space narrowing, and condylar flattening. Discordant cases underwent third-reader adjudication to establish the reference standard. A 3-dimensional ResNet18 model was trained using patient-level training, validation, and independent test partitions. Joint-level OA-associated features were evaluated. Complete TMJ region-of-interest (ROI) and segmentation-masked condyle inputs were compared. Condylar flattening was analyzed separately.

Results

Inter-reader agreement varied by feature, ranging from slight agreement for flattening (κ =  -0.01) and joint-space narrowing (κ = 0.15) to substantial agreement for osteophyte formation (κ = 0.63). Automated condyle segmentation achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 0.91 ± 0.042. The joint-level model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.9325, with sensitivity of 0.8470 and specificity of 0.9081. Feature-level AUCs ranged from 0.6756 to 0.9515. Conclusions

This framework extends CBCT assessment beyond binary detection of TMJ OA-associated changes by providing feature-level characterization. Anatomically guided masking showed higher AUCs for abnormalities intrinsic to the mandibular condyle, whereas joint-space narrowing performed better with broader joint context. These observations require confirmation in larger datasets.

title: Ultrasound-Guided Dorsal Penile Nerve Block Reduces Perioperative Opioid Requirements in Pediatric Circumcision: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Aim This meta-analysis compares ultrasound-guided and landmark-based dorsal penile nerve block (DPNB) in pediatric circumcision. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL from inception to December 2025. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational cohorts comparing ultrasound-guided with landmark-based DPNB in pediatric patients (≤18 years) undergoing circumcision. Primary outcomes were intraoperative and postoperative opioid rescue requirements. Secondary outcomes included pain scores at incision, surgical duration, discharge time, and postoperative nausea/vomiting. Meta-analyses were performed using RStudio version 4.4.3. Results Nine studies involving 949 children met inclusion criteria (five RCTs, four retrospective cohorts). Ultrasound-guided DPNB significantly reduced intraoperative opioid rescue (risk ratio 0.39, 0.18-0.88; p = 0.028) and postoperative opioid requirements (risk ratio 0.26, 0.07-0.94; p = 0.0442) compared with landmark-based techniques. No significant differences emerged in pain scores at incision, discharge time, or postoperative nausea/vomiting. Ultrasound-guided blocks required modestly longer procedural time (mean difference 1.48 min, 0.03-2.94; p = 0.048). Conclusions Ultrasound-guided DPNB substantially may reduce perioperative opioid requirements in pediatric circumcision compared with landmark-based approaches, despite slightly longer procedural times. When resources and expertise permit, ultrasound guidance should be considered the technique of choice for optimizing opioid-sparing anesthesia in this population.

title: Preparation and evaluation of degradable imaging drug loaded embolization microspheres for hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) necessitates the use of embolic agents with intrinsic radiopacity and controlled biodegradability to enhance therapeutic precision. In addressing the limitations inherent in current drug-eluting microspheres (DEMs), this study introduces the development of inherently radiopaque and biodegradable (DOX+Lipiodol) @PLGA @CaCO 3 @Alg core-shell microspheres. These microspheres were synthesized using rotating membrane emulsification and surface-induced ion crosslinking, with calcium carbonate serving multiple roles: a solid surfactant for Pickering stabilization, an acid-neutralizing agent, and an alginate shell inducer. The microspheres successfully encapsulated iodine loads, demonstrated by CT values reaching up to 8,000 HU, and contained doxorubicin at 1.53 ± 0.12 wt.%. They exhibited prolonged radiopacity for over 14 days in vivo and showed a pH-responsive drug release pattern, releasing 90% of their payload at pH 5.2 compared to 30% at pH 7.2 over 120 h. The sequential degradation process (alginate → CaCO 3 → PLGA) resulted in greater than 60% mass loss within four months, correlating with a reduction in CT attenuation. In rabbit embolization models, the microspheres achieved effective vascular occlusion and induced ischemic necrosis in ears and kidneys. CT tracking was possible without additional contrast agents, and systemic biosafety was confirmed with cell viability exceeding 90%, hemolysis below 1%, and normal hematological and histological profiles. These findings suggest that the microspheres could serve as a clinically translatable platform for image-guided TACE, integrating occlusion, therapy, and monitoring into a cohesive treatment strategy.

title: Clinical Features, Multimodal Imaging, and Neurological Differential Diagnoses in Recurrent Susac Syndrome.
abstract: Background Susac's syndrome (SuS) is a rare microangiopathy, often consisting of a classic, pathognomonic, clinical triad of sensorineural hearing impairment, encephalopathy, and retinal arterial occlusions. The variable presentation of SuS leads to underdiagnosis, despite the syndrome standing as an important differential in a variety of ophthalmic, neurological, and psychiatric presentations. Low case numbers and a fast progressive clinical course add to the difficulty of early recognition and treatment. Methods We report on a case of Susac's syndrome in a 40-year-old woman with the classic clinical triad. We report multimodal imaging findings in a patient with recurrent Susac syndrome and discuss these findings in the context of the existing literature. Particular emphasis is placed on neurological differential diagnosis, especially differentiation from multiple sclerosis and other causes of retinal vascular occlusion with nervous system involvement.We summarise the literature of other conditions that can present with retinal vascular occlusion, their associated central nervous system involvement, and imaging changes. Results Multimodal imaging demonstrated branch retinal artery occlusion (BRAO) with corresponding retinal ischaemic changes on optical coherence tomography (OCT) and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), together with characteristic corpus callosal lesions on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The combination of retinal vascular occlusion and central corpus callosal involvement is useful in distinguishing Susac syndrome from important neurological differentials such as multiple sclerosis. Conclusions This case illustrates an example of how combined ophthalmic and neuroimaging findings may support recognition of recurrent Susac syndrome and facilitate distinction from other neurological disorders presenting with retinal vascular occlusion, particularly multiple sclerosis.

title: Multimodal Imaging Characteristics of Sarcoid Retinal Granulomas.
abstract: Purpose To describe the clinical presentation and multimodal imaging characteristics of retinal granulomas in patients with ocular sarcoidosis. Methods In this retrospective observational case series, patients with definite or presumed ocular sarcoidosis presenting with retinal granulomas were evaluated. Multimodal retinal imaging was reviewed to characterize lesion morphology, imaging patterns, and longitudinal evolution. Results Retinal granulomas were identified in three patients with ocular sarcoidosis from diverse racial backgrounds. On fundus photographs, lesions ranged from multiple, superficial, small, faint yellow-gray nodules to more distinct, deeper yellow lesions, predominantly located in the mid- to peripheral retina. All retinal granulomas demonstrated hyperreflectivity on OCT with four distinct morphologic patterns: (1) inner and/or outer retinal granulomas; (2) retinal granulomas associated with retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) disruption and hypertransmission defects; (3) sub-RPE granulomas located between the RPE and Bruch's membrane; and (4) combined chorioretinal granulomas extending from the choroid. FAF demonstrated predominantly isoautofluorescent lesions in the absence of RPE involvement, whereas hypoautofluorescence was observed when the RPE was involved. FA was available for one patient and demonstrated late hyperfluorescent staining of the retinal granulomas. Longitudinal imaging demonstrated evolution from active inflammatory nodules to regression with residual retinal and/or RPE changes, commonly manifesting as punched-out atrophic lesions. Conclusion Retinal granulomas may represent an underrecognized manifestation of ocular sarcoidosis. In our series, multimodal imaging allowed detailed characterization of their morphologic patterns and longitudinal evolution. Recognition of these characteristic imaging features of sarcoid retinal granulomas may facilitate consideration of sarcoidosis in the differential diagnosis of retinal infiltrative lesions.

title: Diagnostic Performance of Deep Learning Models for Ocular Toxoplasmosis Using Fundus Photography: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background Ocular toxoplasmosis (OT) is the leading infectious cause of posterior uveitis worldwide, yet diagnosis remains challenging without a universal gold standard. Although deep learning (DL) shows significant promise for automated image analysis, a rigorous synthesis of its diagnostic accuracy across heterogeneous architectures and datasets is lacking. Methods Following PRISMA-DTA and CLAIM-AI guidelines, we searched major databases through January 2026 for studies evaluating DL models for OT detection using fundus photography. Methodological quality was appraised using QUADAS-2. A bivariate random-effects model (MetaDTA v2.1.3) was applied to pool sensitivity and specificity, generating hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) curves to visualize discriminatory performance. Results Sixteen primary studies (38 model configurations) met qualitative synthesis criteria; nine studies evaluating 24 unique architectures provided sufficient 2×2 contingency data for meta-analysis. Pooled sensitivity was 0.965 (95% CI: 0.944-0.978) and pooled specificity was 0.955 (95% CI: 0.929-0.972). The diagnostic odds ratio reached 594.1 (95% CI: 263.3-1340.4), with positive and negative likelihood ratios of 21.6 and 0.036. Substantial between-study heterogeneity was observed (I^2 = 87.9%). Critically, 81.2% of included studies relied exclusively on a single Paraguayan dataset (OTFID), raising concerns regarding phenotypic bias and limited global generalizability. Conclusion DL models demonstrate excellent diagnostic accuracy for OT on fundus photography, comparable to established ophthalmic AI benchmarks. However, clinical translation is constrained by geographic data homogeneity and the absence of multicentric external validation. Future research must prioritize diverse international cohorts, explainable AI, and federated learning frameworks.

title: Posterior Scleritis Following Uneventful Small-Incision Cataract Surgery.
abstract: Background Posterior scleritis following routine, uncomplicated cataract surgery in a patient without underlying systemic disease is an exceedingly rare and potentially sight-threatening clinical entity. Method A 55-year-old female with no systemic medical history presented three weeks after uneventful small-incision cataract surgery (SICS) in the right eye with sudden vision loss, redness, and severe ocular pain exacerbated by eye movements. Her best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) had deteriorated from 6/9 to finger counting close to her face. Dilated fundus examination revealed multiple dull yellow subretinal lesions across the posterior pole. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showed hyperreflective vitreous cells, subretinal fluid (SRF), and choroidal undulations. B-scan ultrasonography confirmed diffuse posterior scleritis, demonstrating localized sclerochoroidal thickening and fluid accumulation in the sub-Tenon's space. Comprehensive laboratory testing and imaging ruled out infectious and autoimmune etiologies. Result The patient was treated with high-dose intravenous pulse methylprednisolone (1 g/day for three days) followed by an oral prednisolone taper, which led to immediate pain relief and anatomical resolution. At six months, the scleritis had completely resolved with a BCVA improvement to 6/12, limited by persistent localized disruption of the foveal ellipsoid zone on OCT. The patient remained recurrence-free at six months. Conclusion Diffuse posterior scleritis can occur as a postoperative inflammatory phenomenon following uneventful cataract surgery. Clinicians must maintain a high index of suspicion, utilize B-scan ultrasonography for diagnosis, and initiate prompt systemic corticosteroid therapy to optimize anatomical and visual outcomes.

title: Underdetected peripheral artery disease in people with hypertension: A narrative review of risk-stratified case-finding, diagnostic pathways, and equity in care.
abstract: Background Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is common but often underrecognized in people with hypertension because symptoms are frequently absent or atypical and access to physiologic testing is uneven. This narrative review examines how hypertension care can support risk-stratified PAD recognition while keeping targeted case-finding distinct from universal screening. Methods We conducted a structured narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE from inception through 31 July 2026, supplemented by citation searching and review of major US and European guidelines and relevant US policy and coverage sources. Evidence was interpreted according to the question it could answer: association/prognosis, diagnostic accuracy, treatment effect, implementation, or policy status. Results Hypertension and PAD share age-related, metabolic, renal, and tobacco-related determinants, while pressure-related vascular injury provides biological plausibility for their association. Resting ankle-brachial index (ABI) is the initial physiologic test for appropriately selected people; toe-brachial index with waveforms is preferred for noncompressible ankle arteries, exercise ABI for persistent exertional symptoms despite normal or borderline resting values, and duplex ultrasound when anatomic definition will change management. Guideline-supported risk-based testing differs from universal screening of unselected asymptomatic adults, for which outcome benefit remains unproven. Detection is clinically meaningful only when linked to appropriate prevention, symptom management, foot protection, and referral. Conclusion This narrative review supports a risk-stratified, treatment-linked approach to PAD recognition in hypertension care, but the proposed case-finding pathway itself has not been proven to improve clinical outcomes. Pragmatic trials of the complete care pathway are needed.

title: Quantitative assessment of cervical spinal cord injury: Methods, clinical utility, and future directions.
abstract: Study design Literature review. Objectives To provide a structured narrative summary of quantitative assessment methods for cervical spinal cord injury (SCI), analyze their stage-specific applicability, discuss limitations, and clarify the clinical utility and future integration of wearable sensors and artificial intelligence (AI). Methods A narrative review was conducted using PubMed, Web of Science, and EBSCO to identify English-language, peer-reviewed studies published between 1967 and 2026 on quantitative assessment of traumatic and non-traumatic cervical SCI. The search covered imaging, neurological and functional evaluation, electrophysiology, biomechanics, wearable monitoring, artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision, and multimodal data integration. An updated PubMed search performed on May 15, 2026 identified 1,042 records. After title and abstract screening, 873 records were retained as potentially relevant, and 73 unique publications were included in the final narrative synthesis following full-text review and deduplication. Results Main methods include imaging (CT, MRI/DTI, AI-image analysis), neurological scales (ASIA/ISNCSCI, SCIM, WISCI), neuroelectrophysiology (SSEP, MEP, EMG), biomechanics (sEMG and kinematics), and wearable sensors. These methods provide complementary structural, neurological, functional, and real-world activity information across acute care, rehabilitation, and long-term follow-up. Current approaches remain limited by subjectivity, poor real-time monitoring, limited quantification precision, equipment dependence, and insensitivity to early or subclinical changes. originalAbstract:
Study design

Literature review.

Objectives

To provide a structured narrative summary of quantitative assessment methods for cervical spinal cord injury (SCI), analyze their stage-specific applicability, discuss limitations, and clarify the clinical utility and future integration of wearable sensors and artificial intelligence (AI).

Methods

A narrative review was conducted using PubMed, Web of Science, and EBSCO to identify English-language, peer-reviewed studies published between 1967 and 2026 on quantitative assessment of traumatic and non-traumatic cervical SCI. The search covered imaging, neurological and functional evaluation, electrophysiology, biomechanics, wearable monitoring, artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision, and multimodal data integration. An updated PubMed search performed on May 15, 2026 identified 1,042 records. After title and abstract screening, 873 records were retained as potentially relevant, and 73 unique publications were included in the final narrative synthesis following full-text review and deduplication.

Results

Main methods include imaging (CT, MRI/DTI, AI-image analysis), neurological scales (ASIA/ISNCSCI, SCIM, WISCI), neuroelectrophysiology (SSEP, MEP, EMG), biomechanics (sEMG and kinematics), and wearable sensors. These methods provide complementary structural, neurological, functional, and real-world activity information across acute care, rehabilitation, and long-term follow-up. Current approaches remain limited by subjectivity, poor real-time monitoring, limited quantification precision, equipment dependence, and insensitivity to early or subclinical changes. Wearable-AI integration may improve continuous monitoring, risk prediction, pressure injury prevention, and the selection of patients who may benefit from transcutaneous or epidural stimulation.

Conclusion

Current quantitative assessment methods for cervical SCI are insufficient when used alone. A staged, multimodal strategy that combines conventional clinical assessment with wearable sensing and AI-supported analysis may improve full-process management, clinical decision-making, and prognostic assessment in cervical SCI.
